questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the compound obtained when ethyl methyl ketone is treated with $\text{CH}_3\text{MgBr}$ and hydrolyzed.
questions.solution:
Ethyl methyl ketone is $\text{CH}_3-\text{CO}-\text{C}_2\text{H}_5$.

When it reacts with the Grignard reagent $\text{CH}_3\text{MgBr}$, the nucleophilic methyl group attacks the electrophilic carbonyl carbon to form an intermediate alkoxide.

$\text{CH}_3-\text{CO}-\text{C}_2\text{H}_5 + \text{CH}_3\text{MgBr} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3-\text{C}(\text{OMgBr})(\text{CH}_3)-\text{C}_2\text{H}_5$

Upon hydrolysis, the alkoxide is protonated to yield a tertiary alcohol.

$\text{CH}_3-\text{C}(\text{OMgBr})(\text{CH}_3)-\text{C}_2\text{H}_5 \xrightarrow{\text{H}_2\text{O}} \text{C}_2\text{H}_5-\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)_2-\text{OH} + \text{Mg}(\text{OH})\text{Br}$

The final product is 2-methylbutan-2-ol, which matches the structure $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5 - \overset{\overset{\text{CH}_3}{|}}{\underset{\underset{\text{CH}_3}{|}}{\text{C}}} - \text{OH}$.

Answer: $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5 - \overset{\overset{\text{CH}_3}{|}}{\underset{\underset{\text{CH}_3}{|}}{\text{C}}} - \text{OH}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from the following hydroxy compounds contain only one $-\text{OH}$ group in a molecule?
questions.solution:
Crotonyl alcohol (2-buten-1-ol) has the structure $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$, which contains only one $-\text{OH}$ group.

Ethylene glycol (ethane-1,2-diol) has the structure $\text{HO}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{OH}$, which contains two $-\text{OH}$ groups.

Pyrogallol (benzene-1,2,3-triol) contains three $-\text{OH}$ groups attached to a benzene ring.

Hydroquinone (benzene-1,4-diol) contains two $-\text{OH}$ groups attached to a benzene ring.

Therefore, crotonyl alcohol is the only compound among the given options that contains a single $-\text{OH}$ group.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following pair of reagents is used for the conversion of carboxylic acid to alcohol ?
questions.solution:
Carboxylic acids are reduced to primary alcohols by strong reducing agents such as lithium aluminium hydride ($\text{LiAlH}_4$) followed by acid hydrolysis ($\text{H}_3\text{O}^+$).

$\text{RCOOH} \xrightarrow{\text{LiAlH}_4} \text{RCH}_2\text{O}^- \text{Li}^+ \xrightarrow{\text{H}_3\text{O}^+} \text{RCH}_2\text{OH}$

Catalytic hydrogenation using $\text{H}_2 / \text{Ni}$ or $\text{H}_2 / \text{Pd}$ does not reduce carboxylic acids.

$\text{B}_2\text{H}_6 / \text{H}_2\text{O}_2, \text{OH}^-$ is the reagent for the hydroboration-oxidation of alkenes to alcohols.

Answer: $\text{LiAlH}_4 / \text{H}_3\text{O}^+$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following amines is obtained by Gabrial phthalimide synthesis?
questions.solution:
Gabriel phthalimide synthesis is used exclusively for the preparation of primary aliphatic amines.

Phthalimide on treatment with ethanolic potassium hydroxide forms the potassium salt of phthalimide, which on heating with an alkyl halide followed by alkaline hydrolysis produces the corresponding primary amine.

Aromatic primary amines like $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2$ cannot be prepared by this method because aryl halides do not undergo nucleophilic substitution with the phthalimide anion.

Secondary and tertiary amines like $(\text{CH}_3)_2\text{NH}$ and $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{N}(\text{CH}_3)_2$ cannot be prepared by this method.

Among the given options, $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2$ is the only primary aliphatic amine and can be prepared by Gabriel phthalimide synthesis.

Answer: $\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following compounds is obtained when propionamide is treated with $\text{Br}_2$ and concentrated aqueous KOH solution ?
questions.solution:
Propionamide is $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CONH}_2$.

The reaction of an amide with $\text{Br}_2$ and concentrated aqueous KOH is known as the Hoffmann bromamide degradation reaction.

In this reaction, the amide is converted into a primary amine with one carbon atom less than the parent amide.

$\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CONH}_2 + \text{Br}_2 + 4\text{KOH} \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2 + \text{K}_2\text{CO}_3 + 2\text{KBr} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$

The product obtained is ethylamine ($\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$).

Answer: $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following, sugar is an aldohexose?
questions.solution:
Glucose is a monosaccharide containing six carbon atoms and an aldehyde group. Thus, it is an aldohexose.

Ribose is an aldopentose.

Fructose is a ketohexose.

Lactose is a disaccharide.

Answer: Glucose

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following compounds is classified as oligosaccharide?
questions.solution:
Carbohydrates that yield two to ten monosaccharide units on hydrolysis are called oligosaccharides.

Sucrose is a disaccharide, which is a type of oligosaccharide, as it yields one molecule of glucose and one molecule of fructose on hydrolysis.

Ribose, fructose, and glucose are monosaccharides, as they cannot be hydrolyzed further into simpler units of polyhydroxy aldehydes or ketones.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from the following is NOT a monocarboxylic acid?
questions.solution:
Toluic acid is methylbenzoic acid, which contains one $-COOH$ group.

Acrylic acid is propenoic acid ($CH_2=CH-COOH$), which contains one $-COOH$ group.

Phthalic acid is benzene-1,2-dicarboxylic acid ($C_6H_4(COOH)_2$), which contains two $-COOH$ groups. Thus, it is a dicarboxylic acid.

Isobutyric acid is 2-methylpropanoic acid ($(CH_3)_2CH-COOH$), which contains one $-COOH$ group.

Therefore, phthalic acid is not a monocarboxylic acid.

Answer: Phthalic acid

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the number of $sp^3$ hybrid carbon atoms in $\text{HO}(\text{CH}_2)_2\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)_2$?
questions.solution:
The given molecule is 3-methylbutan-1-ol, with the expanded structural formula $\text{HO}-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}(\text{CH}_3)-\text{CH}_3$.

In this structure, every carbon atom is bonded to four other atoms (either carbon, hydrogen, or oxygen) entirely through single ($\sigma$) bonds.

Since there are no $\pi$ bonds present, all the carbon atoms are $sp^3$ hybridized.

Counting the carbon atoms:
Two $-\text{CH}_2-$ groups $\rightarrow 2$ carbon atoms
One $-\text{CH}-$ group $\rightarrow 1$ carbon atom
Two $-\text{CH}_3$ groups $\rightarrow 2$ carbon atoms

Total number of $sp^3$ hybridized carbon atoms $= 2 + 1 + 2 = 5$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify correct order for repulsion between electron pair present in valence shell of central atom of molecule?
questions.solution:
According to VSEPR theory, the electron pairs in the valence shell of the central atom repel each other to minimize electron-electron repulsion.

Lone pairs (Lp) are localized on the central atom and are attracted by only one nucleus, so they occupy more space and exert greater repulsion.

Bond pairs (Bp) are shared between two atoms and are attracted by two nuclei, so they occupy less space and exert lesser repulsion.

Thus, the correct order of repulsion between electron pairs is $\text{Lp-Lp} \gt \text{Lp-Bp} \gt \text{Bp-Bp}$.

Answer: $\text{Lp-Lp} \gt \text{Lp-Bp} \gt \text{Bp-Bp}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which among the following molecule exhibits paramagnetism?
questions.solution:
According to Molecular Orbital Theory, the electronic configuration of $\text{O}_2$ (16 electrons) is:

${\sigma_{1s}}^2 {{\sigma^{*}}_{1s}}^2 \sigma_{2s}^2 {{\sigma^{*}}_{2s}}^2 {\sigma_{2p_z}}^2 {\pi_{2p_x}}^2 {\pi_{2p_y}}^2 {{\pi^{*}}_{2p_x}}^1 {{\pi^{*}}_{2p_y}}^1$

Due to the presence of two unpaired electrons in the degenerate antibonding $\pi^{*}$ molecular orbitals, $\text{O}_2$ is paramagnetic.

$\text{N}_2$ (14 electrons) and $\text{F}_2$ (18 electrons) have all their electrons paired in their molecular orbitals, making them diamagnetic.

$\text{O}_3$ (ozone) also has all its electrons paired and is diamagnetic.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Rate constant of decomposition of hydrogen peroxide is $0.0204\ \text{minutes}^{-1}$, calculate half life of reaction.
questions.solution:
The unit of the rate constant is $\text{minutes}^{-1}$, which indicates that the decomposition of hydrogen peroxide is a first-order reaction.

For a first-order reaction, the half-life is given by:

$t_{1/2} = \dfrac{0.693}{k}$

Substituting the given value of $k = 0.0204\ \text{minutes}^{-1}$:

$t_{1/2} = \dfrac{0.693}{0.0204}$

$t_{1/2} = 33.97\ \text{minutes}$

Answer: $33.97$ minutes

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A first order reaction take $30$ minutes for $75\%$ decomposition, calculate its rate constant ?
questions.solution:
For a first order reaction, the integrated rate law is given by:

$k = \dfrac{2.303}{t} \log \left( \dfrac{a}{a-x} \right)$

Given that the reaction is $75\%$ complete in $30$ minutes:

$t = 30\ \text{minutes}$

$x = 0.75a$

$a - x = a - 0.75a = 0.25a$

Substituting these values into the rate equation:

$k = \dfrac{2.303}{30} \log \left( \dfrac{a}{0.25a} \right)$

$k = \dfrac{2.303}{30} \log (4)$

$k = \dfrac{2.303}{30} \times 0.6020$

$k = \dfrac{1.386}{30} = 0.0462\ \text{minute}^{-1}$

Alternatively, $75\%$ decomposition corresponds to two half-lives:

$t_{75\%} = 2 \times t_{1/2} \Rightarrow 30 = 2 \times t_{1/2} \Rightarrow t_{1/2} = 15\ \text{minutes}$

$k = \dfrac{0.693}{t_{1/2}} = \dfrac{0.693}{15} = 0.0462\ \text{minute}^{-1}$

The closest given option is $0.0463\ \text{minute}^{-1}$.

Answer: $0.0463\ \text{minute}^{-1}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is an elementary reaction ?
questions.solution:
An elementary reaction is one that occurs in a single step and has a single transition state.

The decomposition of ozone, $\text{O}_{3(g)} \rightarrow \text{O}_{2(g)} + \text{O}_{(g)}$, is a unimolecular elementary reaction.

The other reactions are complex and occur in multiple steps:

$2\text{NO}_2\text{Cl}_{(g)} \rightarrow 2\text{NO}_{2(g)} + \text{Cl}_{2(g)}$ occurs via:
$\text{NO}_2\text{Cl} \rightarrow \text{NO}_2 + \text{Cl}$ (slow)
$\text{NO}_2\text{Cl} + \text{Cl} \rightarrow \text{NO}_2 + \text{Cl}_2$ (fast)

$2\text{NO}_{2(g)} + \text{F}_{2(g)} \rightarrow 2\text{NO}_2\text{F}_{(g)}$ occurs via:
$\text{NO}_2 + \text{F}_2 \rightarrow \text{NO}_2\text{F} + \text{F}$ (slow)
$\text{NO}_2 + \text{F} \rightarrow \text{NO}_2\text{F}$ (fast)

$2\text{NO}_{(g)} + \text{Cl}_{2(g)} \rightarrow 2\text{NOCl}_{(g)}$ occurs via:
$\text{NO} + \text{Cl}_2 \rightleftharpoons \text{NOCl}_2$ (fast)
$\text{NOCl}_2 + \text{NO} \rightarrow 2\text{NOCl}$ (slow)

Therefore, only the first reaction is elementary.

Answer: $\text{O}_{3(g)} \rightarrow \text{O}_{2(g)} + \text{O}_{(g)}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify antimicrobial compound from following.
questions.solution:
Cinnamaldehyde is the main active component of cinnamon oil and is widely recognized in chemistry for its strong antimicrobial properties against various bacteria and fungi.

Curcumin is primarily known for its antioxidant properties.

Methyl salicylate is an analgesic used for pain relief.

Ascorbic acid is Vitamin C, which acts primarily as an antioxidant.

Thus, cinnamaldehyde is the antimicrobial compound.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the oxidation state of cobalt in $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_6]^{3+}$ ?
questions.solution:
Let the oxidation state of cobalt be $x$.

Ammonia ($\text{NH}_3$) is a neutral ligand, so its charge is $0$.

The sum of the oxidation states of all atoms in the complex ion is equal to the net charge on the ion.

$x + 6(0) = +3$

$x = +3$

The oxidation state of cobalt in $[\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_6]^{3+}$ is $+3$.

Answer: $+3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What type of hybridization is found in $[\text{Ni}(\text{Cl})_4]^{2-}$?
questions.solution:
The given complex is $[\text{NiCl}_4]^{2-}$.

Let the oxidation state of Ni be $x$.

$x + 4(-1) = -2 \Rightarrow x = +2$

The electronic configuration of neutral Ni is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^8 4s^2$.

The electronic configuration of Ni$^{2+}$ is $[\text{Ar}] 3d^8$.

Cl$^{-}$ is a weak field ligand, so it does not cause the pairing of electrons in the $3d$ orbitals of Ni$^{2+}$.

To accommodate the four electron pairs donated by the four Cl$^{-}$ ligands, the Ni$^{2+}$ ion undergoes hybridization using one $4s$ and three $4p$ empty orbitals.

Therefore, the hybridization involved is $sp^3$, resulting in a tetrahedral geometry.

Answer: $sp^3$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the highest possible oxidation state exhibited by manganese ?
questions.solution:
The atomic number of manganese (Mn) is $25$.

Its electronic configuration is $[Ar] 3d^{5} 4s^{2}$.

The highest oxidation state is achieved when all the valence electrons (both $4s$ and $3d$ electrons) participate in bonding.

Total number of valence electrons $= 5 + 2 = 7$.

Therefore, the highest possible oxidation state exhibited by manganese is $+7$, which is seen in compounds like $KMnO_{4}$ and $Mn_{2}O_{7}$.

Answer: $+7$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify metals present in brass.
questions.solution:
Brass is an alloy composed primarily of copper (Cu) and zinc (Zn).

The proportions of copper and zinc can be varied to create a range of brasses with varying properties.

Answer: Cu and Zn

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify general electronic configuration exhibited by $2^{\text{nd}}$ series of transition elements.
questions.solution:
The second series of transition elements is the $4d$ series, which starts from Yttrium ($Z=39$) and ends at Cadmium ($Z=48$).

The noble gas preceding this series is Krypton ($[\text{Kr}]$, $Z=36$).

The valence electrons are filled in the $4d$ and $5s$ subshells. Due to anomalous configurations (for example, Palladium has the configuration $[\text{Kr}]\ 4d^{10}\ 5s^0$ and elements like Silver have $[\text{Kr}]\ 4d^{10}\ 5s^1$), the number of electrons in the $5s$ orbital can be $0$, $1$, or $2$.

Thus, the general electronic configuration of the $2^{\text{nd}}$ transition series is $[\text{Kr}]\ 4d^{1-10}\ 5s^{0-2}$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: During the electrolysis of aqueous NaCl the product formed at cathode is?
questions.solution:
In the electrolysis of aqueous $\text{NaCl}$, the ions present in the solution are $\text{Na}^{+}$, $\text{Cl}^{-}$, $\text{H}^{+}$, and $\text{OH}^{-}$.

At the cathode, reduction occurs. The competing reactions are:
$\text{Na}^{+} + e^{-} \rightarrow \text{Na}_{(s)}$ ($E^{\circ} = -2.71 \text{ V}$)
$2\text{H}_{2}\text{O}_{(l)} + 2e^{-} \rightarrow \text{H}_{2(g)} + 2\text{OH}^{-}_{(aq)}$ ($E^{\circ} = -0.83 \text{ V}$)

Since the standard reduction potential of water is greater than that of sodium ions, water is preferentially reduced at the cathode.

Thus, hydrogen gas ($\text{H}_{2(g)}$) is liberated at the cathode.

Answer: $\text{H}_{2(g)}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the conductivity of $0.02\ \text{M}\ \text{AgNO}_3$ solution having cell constant $1.2\ \text{cm}^{-1}$ and resistance $95.0\ \text{ohms}$ ?
questions.solution:
Given:

Resistance, $R = 95.0\ \Omega$

Cell constant, $G^{*} = 1.2\ \text{cm}^{-1}$

The conductivity $\kappa$ is given by the relation:

$\kappa = \dfrac{1}{R} \times G^{*}$

Substituting the given values:

$\kappa = \dfrac{1}{95.0} \times 1.2$

$\kappa = 0.01263\ \Omega^{-1}\ \text{cm}^{-1}$

$\kappa = 1.263 \times 10^{-2}\ \Omega^{-1}\ \text{cm}^{-1}$

Answer: $1.263 \times 10^{-2}\ \Omega^{-1}\ \text{cm}^{-1}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is number of moles of electron passed when a current of $2$ Amp flows through solution of electrolyte for $10$ minutes?
questions.solution:
Given, current $I = 2$ A and time $t = 10$ minutes $= 10 \times 60 = 600$ s.

Total charge passed is given by $Q = I \times t$

$Q = 2 \times 600 = 1200$ C

The charge of one mole of electrons is $1$ Faraday ($F \approx 96500$ C).

Number of moles of electrons $= \dfrac{Q}{F}$

Number of moles of electrons $= \dfrac{1200}{96500} = 0.012435$ mol

Number of moles of electrons $\approx 1.243 \times 10^{-2}$ mol

Answer: $1.243 \times 10^{-2}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from the following aldehydes contains two $-\text{CHO}$ groups in a molecule?
questions.solution:
Acrolein is $\text{CH}_2=\text{CH}-\text{CHO}$, which contains one $-\text{CHO}$ group.

o-Tolualdehyde is $o-\text{CH}_3-\text{C}_6\text{H}_4-\text{CHO}$, which contains one $-\text{CHO}$ group.

Phthaldehyde is benzene-1,2-dicarbaldehyde, $\text{C}_6\text{H}_4(\text{CHO})_2$, which contains two $-\text{CHO}$ groups.

Butyraldehyde is $\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}_2-\text{CHO}$, which contains one $-\text{CHO}$ group.

Therefore, phthaldehyde contains two $-\text{CHO}$ groups.

Answer: Phthaldehyde

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from following is a primary benzylic alcohol?
questions.solution:
A benzylic alcohol contains an -OH group attached to an $sp^3$ hybridized carbon atom directly bonded to an aromatic ring.

A primary alcohol has the -OH group attached to a primary carbon atom (a carbon bonded to only one other carbon).

In $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$, the -OH group is attached to a $\text{CH}_2$ group which is directly bonded to the benzene ring. Thus, it is a primary benzylic alcohol.

In $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}(\text{OH})\text{CH}_3$, the -OH group is attached to a secondary carbon, making it a secondary benzylic alcohol.

$\text{H}_2\text{C}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}(\text{OH})\text{CH}_3$ is a secondary allylic alcohol.

$\text{H}_2\text{C}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$ is a primary allylic alcohol.

Answer: $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH}_2\text{OH}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify the aldehyde from following so that the aldehydic group is NOT attached with any $sp^3$ hybrid 'c' atom.
questions.solution:
Methanal is $H-CHO$. The aldehydic group ($-CHO$) is attached to a hydrogen atom, not to any carbon atom. Therefore, it is not attached to any $sp^3$ hybridized carbon atom.

Ethanal is $CH_3-CHO$. The $-CHO$ group is attached to a methyl group, which contains an $sp^3$ hybridized carbon atom.

2-Methylpropanal is $(CH_3)_2CH-CHO$. The $-CHO$ group is attached to a $CH$ group, which is an $sp^3$ hybridized carbon atom.

Propanal is $CH_3-CH_2-CHO$. The $-CHO$ group is attached to a $CH_2$ group, which is an $sp^3$ hybridized carbon atom.

Thus, methanal is the only aldehyde among the given options where the aldehydic group is not attached to an $sp^3$ hybridized carbon atom.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the number of chiral carbon atoms in 2-chlorobutane?
questions.solution:
The structure of 2-chlorobutane is $CH_{3}-CH(Cl)-CH_{2}-CH_{3}$.

A chiral carbon atom is one that is bonded to four different atoms or groups.

In 2-chlorobutane, the second carbon atom (C2) is bonded to four different groups: a hydrogen atom ($-H$), a chlorine atom ($-Cl$), a methyl group ($-CH_{3}$), and an ethyl group ($-CH_{2}CH_{3}$).

Therefore, C2 is a chiral carbon.

The other carbon atoms (C1, C3, and C4) are bonded to at least two identical hydrogen atoms, so they are not chiral.

Thus, there is only $1$ chiral carbon atom in 2-chlorobutane.

Answer: $1$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which from the following compounds is not obtained when methyl bromide is treated with ethyl bromide in presence of sodium metal in dry ether?
questions.solution:
The reaction of methyl bromide and ethyl bromide with sodium metal in dry ether is an example of the Wurtz reaction.

The alkyl free radicals formed during the reaction are methyl radical ($CH_3^{\bullet}$) and ethyl radical ($C_2H_5^{\bullet}$).

These radicals can undergo self-coupling as well as cross-coupling to give a mixture of alkanes:

$CH_3^{\bullet} + CH_3^{\bullet} \rightarrow CH_3-CH_3$ (Ethane)

$C_2H_5^{\bullet} + C_2H_5^{\bullet} \rightarrow CH_3-CH_2-CH_2-CH_3$ (n-Butane)

$CH_3^{\bullet} + C_2H_5^{\bullet} \rightarrow CH_3-CH_2-CH_3$ (Propane)

2-methyl propane cannot be formed by the coupling of methyl and ethyl radicals. Therefore, 2-methyl propane is not obtained in this reaction.

Answer: 2-methyl propane

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following $n$ mole compound is obtained when $2n$ moles of $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{Cl}$ treated of with $2n$ mole sodium atom in dry ether?
questions.solution:
The reaction of an aryl halide with sodium in the presence of dry ether to form a diaryl compound is known as the Fittig reaction.

The chemical equation for the reaction is:

$2\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{Cl} + 2\text{Na} \xrightarrow{\text{dry ether}} \text{C}_6\text{H}_5-\text{C}_6\text{H}_5 + 2\text{NaCl}$

From the stoichiometry of the reaction, $2$ moles of chlorobenzene react with $2$ moles of sodium to produce $1$ mole of biphenyl.

Therefore, $2n$ moles of chlorobenzene reacting with $2n$ moles of sodium will produce $n$ moles of biphenyl.

Answer: Biphenyl

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Identify reagent B in following reaction.
$\text{R}-\text{X} \xrightarrow{\ \large{\text{B}}\ } \text{Nitroalkane}$
questions.solution:
The reaction of an alkyl halide with silver nitrite ($\text{AgNO}_2$) yields a nitroalkane as the major product.

$\text{AgNO}_2$ is predominantly covalent in nature. The bond between silver and oxygen ($\text{Ag}-\text{O}$) is covalent, which leaves the lone pair of electrons on the nitrogen atom available for nucleophilic attack.

Therefore, the nucleophilic attack on the alkyl halide occurs through the nitrogen atom, resulting in the formation of a nitroalkane ($\text{R}-\text{NO}_2$).

In contrast, potassium nitrite ($\text{KNO}_2$) is an ionic compound and provides nitrite ions ($\text{NO}_2^-$) in which oxygen is the nucleophilic center, leading to the formation of alkyl nitrites ($\text{R}-\text{O}-\text{N}=\text{O}$).

Thus, reagent B is $\text{Ag}-\text{O}-\text{N}=\text{O}$.

Answer: $\text{Ag} - \text{O} - \text{N} = \text{O}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the pH of solution containing $5 \times 10^{-4}\ \text{M}\ \text{H}^+$ ion?
questions.solution:
The pH of a solution is given by the negative logarithm of the hydrogen ion concentration:

$\text{pH} = -\log[\text{H}^+]$

Given $[\text{H}^+] = 5 \times 10^{-4}\ \text{M}$

$\text{pH} = -\log(5 \times 10^{-4})$

$\text{pH} = -(\log 5 + \log 10^{-4})$

$\text{pH} = -(\log 5 - 4)$

$\text{pH} = 4 - \log 5$

Using the value $\log 5 \approx 0.699$:

$\text{pH} = 4 - 0.699 = 3.301$

Answer: $3.301$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A weak base is $1.3\%$ dissociated in its aqueous solution. If $K_b$ for weak base is $1.69 \times 10^{-5}$ at $298$ K. Find the concentration of aqueous solution of weak base.
questions.solution:
For a weak base, the dissociation constant $K_b$ is given by Ostwald's dilution law:

$K_b = \dfrac{C \alpha^2}{1 - \alpha}$

Since the degree of dissociation $\alpha = 1.3\% = 0.013$ is very small ($\alpha \ll 1$), we can approximate $1 - \alpha \approx 1$. The expression simplifies to:

$K_b = C \alpha^2$

Rearranging for concentration $C$:

$C = \dfrac{K_b}{\alpha^2}$

Substituting the given values $K_b = 1.69 \times 10^{-5}$ and $\alpha = 0.013$:

$C = \dfrac{1.69 \times 10^{-5}}{(0.013)^2}$

$C = \dfrac{1.69 \times 10^{-5}}{1.69 \times 10^{-4}}$

$C = 10^{-1} = 0.1$ M

Answer: $0.1$ M

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which among the following oxoacids of chlorine exhibits $+3$ oxidation state of chlorine?
questions.solution:
Let the oxidation state of chlorine be $x$.

In $\text{HClO}$:
$+1 + x - 2 = 0 \Rightarrow x = +1$

In $\text{HClO}_2$:
$+1 + x + 2(-2) = 0 \Rightarrow x = +3$

In $\text{HClO}_3$:
$+1 + x + 3(-2) = 0 \Rightarrow x = +5$

In $\text{HClO}_4$:
$+1 + x + 4(-2) = 0 \Rightarrow x = +7$

Chlorine exhibits a $+3$ oxidation state in $\text{HClO}_2$.

Answer: $\text{HClO}_2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify thermosetting polymer from following.
questions.solution:
Thermosetting polymers are cross-linked or heavily branched molecules, which on heating undergo extensive cross-linking in moulds and become infusible. These cannot be reused.

Examples of thermosetting polymers include Bakelite, urea-formaldehyde resins, and melamine-formaldehyde resins.

Polystyrene is a thermoplastic polymer.

Buna-S is an elastomer.

Terylene is a fibre.

Answer: Ureaformaldehyde resin

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify ureaformaldehyde resin from following polymers?
questions.solution:
Urea-formaldehyde resin is a condensation polymer formed by the reaction between urea ($NH_2-CO-NH_2$) and formaldehyde ($HCHO$).

The initial reaction involves the formation of methylol urea derivatives, which then undergo condensation with the elimination of water molecules to form a cross-linked polymer network.

The repeating unit of the urea-formaldehyde polymer chain is derived from linking the nitrogen atoms of urea with the methylene ($-CH_2-$) group from formaldehyde.

The repeating unit is $[-NH-CO-NH-CH_2-]_n$.

Let us analyze the other options:
Option (1) is polyacrylamide.
Option (2) is polystyrene.
Option (4) is nylon-6, which is polycaprolactam.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Identify change in oxidation state of oxidising agent in following redox reaction.
$3\text{H}_3\text{AsO}_{3(aq)} + \text{BrO}_{3(aq)}^- \longrightarrow \text{Br}_{(aq)}^- + 3\text{H}_3\text{AsO}_{4(aq)}$
questions.solution:
The given reaction is $3\text{H}_3\text{AsO}_{3(aq)} + \text{BrO}_{3(aq)}^- \longrightarrow \text{Br}_{(aq)}^- + 3\text{H}_3\text{AsO}_{4(aq)}$

Let the oxidation state of As in $\text{H}_3\text{AsO}_3$ be $x$.
$3(+1) + x + 3(-2) = 0 \Rightarrow x = +3$

Let the oxidation state of Br in $\text{BrO}_3^-$ be $y$.
$y + 3(-2) = -1 \Rightarrow y = +5$

Let the oxidation state of As in $\text{H}_3\text{AsO}_4$ be $z$.
$3(+1) + z + 4(-2) = 0 \Rightarrow z = +5$

The oxidation state of Br in $\text{Br}^-$ is $-1$.

The oxidation state of As increases from $+3$ to $+5$, so $\text{H}_3\text{AsO}_3$ undergoes oxidation and acts as a reducing agent.

The oxidation state of Br decreases from $+5$ to $-1$, so $\text{BrO}_3^-$ undergoes reduction and acts as an oxidising agent.

The change in oxidation state of the oxidising agent is $+5$ to $-1$.

Answer: $+5\ \text{to}\ -1$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which element from following forms superoxide with oxygen?
questions.solution:
Alkali metals react with oxygen to form different types of oxides depending on their size.

Lithium forms mainly monoxide ($Li_{2}O$).

Sodium forms mainly peroxide ($Na_{2}O_{2}$).

Potassium, rubidium, and cesium form mainly superoxides ($MO_{2}$) due to the stabilization of the large superoxide ion by large cations.

Magnesium forms mainly monoxide ($MgO$).

Therefore, potassium forms a superoxide with oxygen.

Answer: Potassium

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the number of tetrahedral voids present in $0.5$ mole of compound forming hcp structure?
questions.solution:
Number of atoms in $0.5$ mole of the compound $= 0.5 \times N_A = 0.5 \times 6.022 \times 10^{23} = 3.011 \times 10^{23}$.

In a close-packed structure, the number of tetrahedral voids is twice the number of atoms forming the lattice.

Number of tetrahedral voids $= 2 \times 3.011 \times 10^{23} = 6.022 \times 10^{23}$.

Answer: $6.022 \times 10^{23}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Gold crystallizes as fcc unit cell, the edge length of unit cell is $408$ pm. What is the radius of gold atom?
questions.solution:
For a face-centered cubic (fcc) unit cell, the relationship between the edge length $a$ and the radius of the atom $r$ is given by:

$4r = \sqrt{2}a$

$r = \dfrac{a}{2\sqrt{2}}$

Given $a = 408$ pm:

$r = \dfrac{408}{2\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{204}{\sqrt{2}} = 102\sqrt{2}$ pm

Substituting $\sqrt{2} = 1.414$:

$r = 102 \times 1.414 = 144.228$ pm $\approx 144.2$ pm

Answer: $144.2$ pm

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: van't Hoff factor for $\text{BaCl}_2$ is $2.47$, calculate the percentage dissociation of in its aqueous solution.
questions.solution:
The dissociation reaction of $\text{BaCl}_2$ is:

$\text{BaCl}_2 \rightleftharpoons \text{Ba}^{2+} + 2\text{Cl}^{-}$

The number of ions produced per formula unit, $n = 3$.

The relation between van't Hoff factor $i$ and degree of dissociation $\alpha$ is:

$i = 1 + (n - 1)\alpha$

Substituting the given values:

$2.47 = 1 + (3 - 1)\alpha$

$2.47 = 1 + 2\alpha$

$2\alpha = 1.47$

$\alpha = 0.735$

Percentage dissociation $= \alpha \times 100 = 73.5\%$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A solution of non volatile solute has boiling point elevation $0.70$ K if $K_b$ for the solvent is $2.44\ \text{K kg mol}^{-1}$. What is the molality of the solution?
questions.solution:
The elevation in boiling point is given by the formula:

$\Delta T_b = K_b \times m$

where $\Delta T_b$ is the boiling point elevation, $K_b$ is the ebullioscopic constant, and $m$ is the molality of the solution.

Given:
$\Delta T_b = 0.70$ K
$K_b = 2.44$ K kg mol$^{-1}$

Substituting the given values into the formula:

$0.70 = 2.44 \times m$

$m = \dfrac{0.70}{2.44}$

$m \approx 0.286$ m

Answer: $0.286$ m

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which among the following pairs of solutions is isotonic in nature?
questions.solution:
Isotonic solutions are those which have the same osmotic pressure at a given temperature.

Osmotic pressure is given by $\pi = iCRT$, where $i$ is the van't Hoff factor, $C$ is the molar concentration, $R$ is the gas constant, and $T$ is the temperature.

For two solutions to be isotonic, their effective concentrations must be equal: $i_1C_1 = i_2C_2$.

For $0.1$ M urea and $0.1$ M sucrose:
Urea is a non-electrolyte, so $i = 1$. Effective concentration $= 1 \times 0.1 = 0.1$ M.
Sucrose is a non-electrolyte, so $i = 1$. Effective concentration $= 1 \times 0.1 = 0.1$ M.
Since $i_1C_1 = i_2C_2$, these two solutions are isotonic.

For $0.1$ M urea and $0.1$ M KCl:
KCl dissociates into $K^+$ and $Cl^-$, so $i = 2$. Effective concentration $= 2 \times 0.1 = 0.2$ M.
They are not isotonic.

For $0.1$ M KCl and $0.1$ M $\text{CaCl}_2$:
$\text{CaCl}_2$ dissociates into $Ca^{2+}$ and $2Cl^-$, so $i = 3$. Effective concentration $= 3 \times 0.1 = 0.3$ M.
They are not isotonic.

Answer: $0.1$ M urea and $0.1$ M sucrose

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What quantity of $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ in gram is present in $0.25$ mol of it?
questions.solution:
Molar mass of $\text{H}_2\text{O} = 2 \times 1 + 16 = 18 \text{ g/mol}$

Mass of $\text{H}_2\text{O} = \text{moles} \times \text{molar mass}$

Mass $= 0.25 \times 18 = 4.5 \text{ g}$

Answer: $4.5$ g

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the percentage atom economy when formula weight of product is $65$ u and the sum of formula weight of reactant is $130$ u?
questions.solution:
The percentage atom economy is calculated using the formula:

$\text{Percentage atom economy} = \dfrac{\text{Formula weight of desired product}}{\text{Sum of formula weights of all reactants}} \times 100$

Substituting the given values:

$\text{Percentage atom economy} = \dfrac{65}{130} \times 100 = 50\%$

Answer: $50\%$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following is not an illustration of viscosity?
options: Thickening of glass panes of old buildings
questions.solution:
Gradation of lubricant oils is done on the basis of their viscosity.

High viscosity of blood is an indicator of cardiovascular diseases.

Glass is a supercooled liquid with very high viscosity, which causes it to flow downwards very slowly over time, resulting in the thickening of glass panes at the bottom in old buildings.

The cleansing action of soap is based on the principle of surface tension, not viscosity. Soap lowers the surface tension of water, allowing it to spread and penetrate more easily.

Answer: Cleansing action of soap

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the wave number of lowest transition associated with Paschen series?
questions.solution:
The wave number $\bar{v}$ for a transition in a hydrogen atom is given by the Rydberg formula:

$\bar{v} = R_H \left( \dfrac{1}{n_1^2} - \dfrac{1}{n_2^2} \right)$

For the Paschen series, the lower energy level is $n_1 = 3$.

The lowest transition corresponds to the minimum energy difference, which occurs for the transition from the immediately higher energy level, $n_2 = 4$.

Substituting these values into the formula:

$\bar{v} = R_H \left( \dfrac{1}{3^2} - \dfrac{1}{4^2} \right)$

$\bar{v} = R_H \left( \dfrac{1}{9} - \dfrac{1}{16} \right)$

$\bar{v} = R_H \left( \dfrac{16 - 9}{144} \right)$

$\bar{v} = R_H \left( \dfrac{7}{144} \right) \text{cm}^{-1}$

Answer: $R_H\left(\dfrac{7}{144}\right)\ \text{cm}^{-1}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following properties of colloid is used to measure the rate of migration of sol particles?
questions.solution:
Electrophoresis is the phenomenon of movement of colloidal particles under the influence of an applied electric field. By observing this movement, the rate of migration of sol particles can be measured.

Tyndall effect is the scattering of light by colloidal particles.

Brownian motion is the continuous zig-zag motion of colloidal particles.

Electroosmosis is the movement of the dispersion medium under an electric field when the colloidal particles are prevented from moving.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An ideal gas expands from initial volume $5\ \text{dm}^3$ to $15\ \text{dm}^3$ against a constant external pressure of $2$ atm. What is the work done by the gas ?
questions.solution:
The work done by a gas during expansion against a constant external pressure is given by the formula:

$W = -P_{\text{ext}} \Delta V$

Given:
$P_{\text{ext}} = 2\ \text{atm}$
$V_i = 5\ \text{dm}^3 = 5\ \text{L}$
$V_f = 15\ \text{dm}^3 = 15\ \text{L}$

Change in volume:
$\Delta V = V_f - V_i = 15 - 5 = 10\ \text{L}$

Substituting the values into the formula:
$W = -2\ \text{atm} \times 10\ \text{L} = -20\ \text{L}\ \text{atm}$

To convert the work done into Joules, use the conversion factor $1\ \text{L}\ \text{atm} = 101.32\ \text{J}$:
$W = -20 \times 101.32\ \text{J} = -2026.4\ \text{J}$

Answer: $-2026.4$ J

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A gas absorbs $120$ J of heat and expands by $300 \times 10^{-6}\ \text{m}^3$ against a constant external pressure of $2 \times 10^5\ \text{Nm}^{-2}$. What will be the change in internal energy of the system ?
questions.solution:
Heat absorbed by the gas, $q = +120\ \text{J}$

Work done by the gas during expansion against constant external pressure is given by $W = -P_{\text{ext}} \Delta V$

Substituting the given values:

$W = -(2 \times 10^5\ \text{Nm}^{-2}) \times (300 \times 10^{-6}\ \text{m}^3)$

$W = -60\ \text{J}$

According to the first law of thermodynamics:

$\Delta U = q + W$

$\Delta U = 120\ \text{J} - 60\ \text{J} = 60\ \text{J}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Identify from following, the relation between standard free energy change in a reaction and equilibrium constant $K_c$.
questions.solution:
The relation between the free energy change and the reaction quotient is given by $\Delta G = \Delta G^\circ + RT \ln Q$.

At equilibrium, the free energy change $\Delta G = 0$ and the reaction quotient $Q = K_c$.

Substituting these values into the equation, we get $0 = \Delta G^\circ + RT \ln K_c$.

Rearranging the terms yields $-\Delta G^\circ = RT \ln K_c$.

Answer: $-\triangle G^\circ = RT \ln K_c$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The value of $c$ satisfied by the Rolle's theorem for the function $f(x) = x^2(1 - x)^2$, $x \in [0, 1]$ is...
questions.solution:
Given function is $f(x) = x^2(1 - x)^2$ on the interval $[0, 1]$.

The function is a polynomial, so it is continuous on $[0, 1]$ and differentiable on $(0, 1)$.

Also, $f(0) = 0$ and $f(1) = 0$, so $f(0) = f(1)$.

By Rolle's theorem, there exists at least one $c \in (0, 1)$ such that $f'(c) = 0$.

Differentiating $f(x)$ with respect to $x$:

$f'(x) = \dfrac{d}{dx}[x^2(1 - x)^2] = 2x(1 - x)^2 + x^2 \cdot 2(1 - x)(-1)$

$f'(x) = 2x(1 - x)[(1 - x) - x] = 2x(1 - x)(1 - 2x)$

Setting $f'(c) = 0$:

$2c(1 - c)(1 - 2c) = 0$

The possible values are $c = 0$, $c = 1$, and $c = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

Since $c$ must lie in the open interval $(0, 1)$, the only valid value is $c = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{2}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A particle is fired straight up from the ground. Its height in feet after $t$ second is given by $s(t) = 128t - 16t^2$. The velocity of the particle when it hits the ground is...
questions.solution:
The height of the particle is given by $s(t) = 128t - 16t^2$.

The particle hits the ground when $s(t) = 0$.

$128t - 16t^2 = 0$

$16t(8 - t) = 0$

This gives $t = 0$ or $t = 8$. The particle hits the ground at $t = 8$ seconds.

The velocity of the particle is given by the derivative of the position function:

$v(t) = \dfrac{ds}{dt} = 128 - 32t$

Substituting $t = 8$ into the velocity equation:

$v(8) = 128 - 32(8) = 128 - 256 = -128$ ft/sec.

Answer: $-128$ ft/sec

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A tank with a rectangular base and rectangular sides, open at the top is made. Depth of the tank is $4$ m and its volume is $36$ cubic meters. For making a tank cost of base material used is Rs. $100$ per sq. meter and that of sides is Rs. $50$ per sq. meter. Then minimum cost of tank is ..............
questions.solution:
Let the length and breadth of the base of the tank be $x$ and $y$ respectively.

Given depth $h = 4$ m and volume $V = 36$ m$^3$.

$V = x \times y \times h \Rightarrow 4xy = 36 \Rightarrow xy = 9$

Cost of the base $= 100 \times xy = 100 \times 9 = 900$

Area of the four sides $= 2(xh + yh) = 2(4)(x + y) = 8(x + y)$

Cost of the sides $= 50 \times 8(x + y) = 400(x + y)$

Total cost $C = 900 + 400(x + y)$

To minimize $C$, we need to minimize $x + y$.

Using AM-GM inequality for $x, y \gt 0$:

$\dfrac{x + y}{2} \geq \sqrt{xy}$

$x + y \geq 2\sqrt{9} = 6$

Minimum value of $x + y$ is $6$, which occurs when $x = y = 3$.

Minimum cost $C = 900 + 400(6) = 900 + 2400 = 3300$

Answer: Rs. $3300$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The area (in sq. units) of the region enclosed by $\{(x, y) \mid y \leq x^2, xy \leq 8, y \geq 1\}$ is...
questions.solution:
The region is bounded by the curves $y = x^2$, $xy = 8$, and $y = 1$ in the first quadrant (as the area must be finite).

To find the intersection points of the curves:
Intersection of $y = x^2$ and $xy = 8$:
$x(x^2) = 8 \Rightarrow x^3 = 8 \Rightarrow x = 2$
At $x = 2$, $y = 4$.

Intersection of $y = x^2$ and $y = 1$:
$x^2 = 1 \Rightarrow x = 1$ (taking $x \gt 0$).

Intersection of $xy = 8$ and $y = 1$:
$x(1) = 8 \Rightarrow x = 8$.

The area can be calculated by integrating with respect to $y$ from $y = 1$ to $y = 4$. For a given $y$, the value of $x$ ranges from the parabola $x = \sqrt{y}$ to the hyperbola $x = \dfrac{8}{y}$.

Required Area $= \displaystyle \int_{1}^{4} \left( \dfrac{8}{y} - \sqrt{y} \right) dy$

$= \left[ 8 \log y - \dfrac{2}{3} y^{3/2} \right]_{1}^{4}$

$= \left( 8 \log 4 - \dfrac{2}{3} (4)^{3/2} \right) - \left( 8 \log 1 - \dfrac{2}{3} (1)^{3/2} \right)$

$= \left( 16 \log 2 - \dfrac{2}{3} (8) \right) - \left( 0 - \dfrac{2}{3} \right)$

$= 16 \log 2 - \dfrac{16}{3} + \dfrac{2}{3}$

$= 16 \log 2 - \dfrac{14}{3}$

Answer: $16\log 2 - \dfrac{14}{3}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If the area of the region bounded by the parabola $y^2 = 4kx$ and the line $x = k$, (where $k  \gt  0$) is $\dfrac{128}{3}$ sq. units, then the value of $\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{2}{k}\right)$ is equal to...
questions.solution:
The area of the region bounded by the parabola $y^2 = 4kx$ and the line $x = k$ is given by

$A = 2 \int_{0}^{k} y \, dx$

$A = 2 \int_{0}^{k} \sqrt{4kx} \, dx$

$A = 4\sqrt{k} \left[ \dfrac{2}{3} x^{3/2} \right]_{0}^{k}$

$A = \dfrac{8}{3} k^2$

Given that the area is $\dfrac{128}{3}$, we have

$\dfrac{8}{3} k^2 = \dfrac{128}{3}$

$k^2 = 16$

Since $k \gt 0$, we get $k = 4$.

Substituting $k = 4$:

$\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{2}{k}\right) = \sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{2}{4}\right) = \sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$

Answer: $\dfrac{\pi}{6}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The smallest positive integer $n$ for which $\dfrac{(1 + i)^n}{(1 - i)^{n-2}}$ is a real number, is ...
questions.solution:
The given expression is $\dfrac{(1 + i)^n}{(1 - i)^{n-2}}$.

This can be rewritten as $\left(\dfrac{1 + i}{1 - i}\right)^n (1 - i)^2$.

Simplifying the term inside the bracket:

$\dfrac{1 + i}{1 - i} = \dfrac{(1 + i)^2}{(1 - i)(1 + i)} = \dfrac{1 + i^2 + 2i}{1^2 - i^2} = \dfrac{2i}{2} = i$

Simplifying the second term:

$(1 - i)^2 = 1 + i^2 - 2i = -2i$

Substituting these back into the expression, we get:

$i^n (-2i) = -2 i^{n+1}$

For this expression to be a real number, $i^{n+1}$ must be a real number. This is possible only when the exponent $n+1$ is an even integer.

$n + 1 = 2k$, where $k$ is an integer.

$n = 2k - 1$

To find the smallest positive integer $n$, substitute $k = 1$:

$n = 2(1) - 1 = 1$

Answer: $1$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The value of $\displaystyle\int_2^4 (\{x\} + [x])\,dx =$...(where $\{x\}$ and $[x]$ are the fractional part function and the greatest integer function, respectively)
questions.solution:
By the definition of the fractional part and greatest integer functions, $x = [x] + \{x\}$.

Substituting this into the integral:

$\displaystyle\int_2^4 (\{x\} + [x])\,dx = \displaystyle\int_2^4 x\,dx$

Evaluating the definite integral:

$\displaystyle\int_2^4 x\,dx = \left[ \dfrac{x^2}{2} \right]_2^4$

$= \dfrac{16}{2} - \dfrac{4}{2}$

$= 8 - 2 = 6$

Answer: $6$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $[x]$ is the greatest integer function not greater than $x$, then the value of $\displaystyle\int_0^2 x[x^2]\,dx$ is...
questions.solution:
Let $I = \displaystyle\int_0^2 x[x^2]\,dx$

Substitute $x^2 = t \Rightarrow 2x\,dx = dt \Rightarrow x\,dx = \dfrac{dt}{2}$

When $x = 0$, $t = 0$ and when $x = 2$, $t = 4$

$I = \dfrac{1}{2} \displaystyle\int_0^4 [t]\,dt$

$I = \dfrac{1}{2} \left( \displaystyle\int_0^1 0\,dt + \displaystyle\int_1^2 1\,dt + \displaystyle\int_2^3 2\,dt + \displaystyle\int_3^4 3\,dt \right)$

$I = \dfrac{1}{2} (0 + 1(2-1) + 2(3-2) + 3(4-3))$

$I = \dfrac{1}{2} (1 + 2 + 3) = \dfrac{6}{2} = 3$

Answer: $3$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The solution of the differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{a + bx}{c + dy}$ represents a family of circles centered at the origin if...
questions.solution:
The equation of a family of circles centered at the origin is given by $x^2 + y^2 = r^2$, where $r$ is an arbitrary constant.

Differentiating this equation with respect to $x$, we get:

$2x + 2y \dfrac{dy}{dx} = 0$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = -\dfrac{x}{y}$

The given differential equation is:

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{a + bx}{c + dy}$

For this to represent the family of circles centered at the origin, it must be identical to $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = -\dfrac{x}{y}$.

Comparing the two equations, we get:

$\dfrac{a + bx}{c + dy} = \dfrac{-x}{y}$

This requires $a = 0$ and $c = 0$. The equation then becomes:

$\dfrac{bx}{dy} = -\dfrac{x}{y}$

$\dfrac{b}{d} = -1$

$b = -d \Rightarrow b + d = 0$

Thus, the required conditions are $a = c = 0$ and $b + d = 0$.

Answer: $a = c = 0,\ b + d = 0$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The solution of the differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{x - y}{x + y}$, when $x = 0$ and $y = 0$ represents ....
questions.solution:
The given differential equation is $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{x - y}{x + y}$

Rearranging the terms, we get:

$(x + y)dy = (x - y)dx$

$x dy + y dy = x dx - y dx$

$x dy + y dx = x dx - y dy$

This can be written as exact differentials:

$d(xy) = x dx - y dy$

Integrating both sides, we get:

$\int d(xy) = \int x dx - \int y dy$

$xy = \dfrac{x^2}{2} - \dfrac{y^2}{2} + C$

$x^2 - 2xy - y^2 = -2C$

Given that $x = 0$ when $y = 0$, substituting these values gives:

$0^2 - 2(0)(0) - 0^2 = -2C \Rightarrow C = 0$

Substituting $C = 0$ back into the equation, we obtain:

$x^2 - 2xy - y^2 = 0$

This is a homogeneous equation of degree 2 in $x$ and $y$ (of the form $ax^2 + 2hxy + by^2 = 0$), which represents a pair of straight lines passing through the origin.

Answer: Pair of straight Lines

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The derivative of $\log_{10} x$ with respect to $\log_x 10$ is
questions.solution:
Let $u = \log_{10} x$ and $v = \log_x 10$.

Using the base change property of logarithms, $v = \dfrac{1}{\log_{10} x} = \dfrac{1}{u}$.

Differentiating $v$ with respect to $u$, we get $\dfrac{dv}{du} = -\dfrac{1}{u^2}$.

The derivative of $u$ with respect to $v$ is given by $\dfrac{du}{dv} = \dfrac{1}{\dfrac{dv}{du}}$.

Substituting the value of $\dfrac{dv}{du}$, we get $\dfrac{du}{dv} = -u^2$.

Replacing $u$ with $\log_{10} x$, we obtain $\dfrac{du}{dv} = -(\log_{10} x)^2$.

Answer: $-(\log_{10} x)^2$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $y = \cot^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1 + \sin 5x}{\cos 5x}\right)$, then the value of $\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ is
questions.solution:
Given $y = \cot^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1 + \sin 5x}{\cos 5x}\right)$

We can simplify the expression inside the inverse trigonometric function using half-angle formulas:

$\dfrac{1 + \sin 5x}{\cos 5x} = \dfrac{\left(\cos \dfrac{5x}{2} + \sin \dfrac{5x}{2}\right)^2}{\cos^2 \dfrac{5x}{2} - \sin^2 \dfrac{5x}{2}}$

$\Rightarrow \dfrac{1 + \sin 5x}{\cos 5x} = \dfrac{\cos \dfrac{5x}{2} + \sin \dfrac{5x}{2}}{\cos \dfrac{5x}{2} - \sin \dfrac{5x}{2}}$

Dividing the numerator and the denominator by $\cos \dfrac{5x}{2}$:

$\dfrac{1 + \sin 5x}{\cos 5x} = \dfrac{1 + \tan \dfrac{5x}{2}}{1 - \tan \dfrac{5x}{2}} = \tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4} + \dfrac{5x}{2}\right)$

Using the complementary angle identity $\tan \theta = \cot\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - \theta\right)$:

$\tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4} + \dfrac{5x}{2}\right) = \cot\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2} - \left(\dfrac{\pi}{4} + \dfrac{5x}{2}\right)\right) = \cot\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4} - \dfrac{5x}{2}\right)$

Substituting this back into the original equation:

$y = \cot^{-1}\left[\cot\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4} - \dfrac{5x}{2}\right)\right]$

$y = \dfrac{\pi}{4} - \dfrac{5x}{2}$

Differentiating with respect to $x$:

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{d}{dx}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4} - \dfrac{5x}{2}\right) = -\dfrac{5}{2}$

Answer: $-\dfrac{5}{2}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Let $x = at^2 - 1$, where $a  \gt  0$ and $y = t^3 + 1$. If at $t = 1$, $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = \dfrac{3}{16}$, then the value of $a$ is...
questions.solution:
Given $x = at^2 - 1$ and $y = t^3 + 1$

Differentiating with respect to $t$, we get

$\dfrac{dx}{dt} = 2at$ and $\dfrac{dy}{dt} = 3t^2$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{\dfrac{dy}{dt}}{\dfrac{dx}{dt}} = \dfrac{3t^2}{2at} = \dfrac{3t}{2a}$

Differentiating again with respect to $x$, we get

$\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = \dfrac{d}{dt}\left(\dfrac{3t}{2a}\right) \cdot \dfrac{dt}{dx}$

$\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = \dfrac{3}{2a} \cdot \dfrac{1}{2at} = \dfrac{3}{4a^2t}$

At $t = 1$, $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = \dfrac{3}{4a^2}$

Given that at $t = 1$, $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2} = \dfrac{3}{16}$

$\dfrac{3}{4a^2} = \dfrac{3}{16}$

$4a^2 = 16 \Rightarrow a^2 = 4$

Since $a \gt 0$, we get $a = 2$

Answer: $2$

questions.q: If $y = \sin(2\sin^{-1} x)$ then $\dfrac{dy}{dx} =$..
questions.solution:
Given $y = \sin(2\sin^{-1} x)$

Differentiating with respect to $x$ using the chain rule:

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \cos(2\sin^{-1} x) \cdot \dfrac{d}{dx}(2\sin^{-1} x)$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \cos(2\sin^{-1} x) \cdot \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{1 - x^2}}$

Using the trigonometric identity $\cos(2\theta) = 1 - 2\sin^2\theta$, we can write:

$\cos(2\sin^{-1} x) = 1 - 2\sin^2(\sin^{-1} x) = 1 - 2x^2$

Substituting this back into the derivative:

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = (1 - 2x^2) \cdot \dfrac{2}{\sqrt{1 - x^2}}$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = \dfrac{2 - 4x^2}{\sqrt{1 - x^2}}$

questions.q: A tangent having slope $-\dfrac{1}{2}$ to the ellipse $3x^2 + 4y^2 = 12$ intersects the X-axis and Y-axis at the points A and B respectively. if O is the origin, then the area of $\triangle AOB$ is ...
questions.solution:
The equation of the given ellipse can be rewritten as $\dfrac{x^2}{4} + \dfrac{y^2}{3} = 1$

Here, $a^2 = 4$ and $b^2 = 3$

The equation of a tangent to the ellipse with slope $m$ is given by $y = mx \pm \sqrt{a^2m^2 + b^2}$

Given the slope $m = -\dfrac{1}{2}$, substituting the values we get:

$y = -\dfrac{1}{2}x \pm \sqrt{4\left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^2 + 3}$

$y = -\dfrac{1}{2}x \pm \sqrt{1 + 3}$

$y = -\dfrac{1}{2}x \pm 2$

$x + 2y = \pm 4$

The tangent intersects the X-axis at $A(\pm 4, 0)$ and the Y-axis at $B(0, \pm 2)$

The area of $\triangle AOB$ is $\dfrac{1}{2} \times OA \times OB = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 4 \times 2 = 4$ sq. units

Answer: $4$ sq. units

questions.q: If $f(x) = x^2$ and $g(x) = [x^2]$ where $[\cdot]$ represents the greatest integer function then, $(f \circ g)\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right) + (g \circ f)\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right)$ is equal to ...
questions.solution:
Given $f(x) = x^2$ and $g(x) = [x^2]$.

First, evaluating $(f \circ g)\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right)$:

$g\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right) = \left[\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right)^2\right] = \left[\dfrac{9}{4}\right] = [2.25] = 2$

$f\left(g\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right)\right) = f(2) = 2^2 = 4$

Next, evaluating $(g \circ f)\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right)$:

$f\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right) = \left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right)^2 = \dfrac{9}{4}$

$g\left(f\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right)\right) = g\left(\dfrac{9}{4}\right) = \left[\left(\dfrac{9}{4}\right)^2\right] = \left[\dfrac{81}{16}\right] = [5.0625] = 5$

Adding both values:

$(f \circ g)\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right) + (g \circ f)\left(\dfrac{3}{2}\right) = 4 + 5 = 9$

Answer: $9$

questions.q: If $\displaystyle\int \dfrac{dx}{x^{7/2}(x^4 + 1)^{3/8}} = m\left(\dfrac{x^4 + 1}{x^4}\right)^n + c$, where $c$ is a constant of integration, then the value of $\dfrac{n}{m}$ is...
questions.solution:
Given integral is $I = \displaystyle\int \dfrac{dx}{x^{7/2}(x^4 + 1)^{3/8}}$

Factoring out $x^4$ from the term $(x^4 + 1)^{3/8}$, we get:

$I = \displaystyle\int \dfrac{dx}{x^{7/2} \cdot (x^4)^{3/8} \left(1 + \dfrac{1}{x^4}\right)^{3/8}}$

$I = \displaystyle\int \dfrac{dx}{x^{7/2} \cdot x^{3/2} (1 + x^{-4})^{3/8}}$

$I = \displaystyle\int \dfrac{dx}{x^5 (1 + x^{-4})^{3/8}}$

Let $1 + x^{-4} = t$

Differentiating both sides, we get:

$-4x^{-5} dx = dt \Rightarrow \dfrac{dx}{x^5} = -\dfrac{dt}{4}$

Substituting this into the integral:

$I = -\dfrac{1}{4} \displaystyle\int t^{-3/8} dt$

$I = -\dfrac{1}{4} \left( \dfrac{t^{5/8}}{5/8} \right) + c$

$I = -\dfrac{2}{5} t^{5/8} + c$

Substituting back $t = 1 + x^{-4} = \dfrac{x^4 + 1}{x^4}$:

$I = -\dfrac{2}{5} \left( \dfrac{x^4 + 1}{x^4} \right)^{5/8} + c$

Comparing this with the given expression $m\left(\dfrac{x^4 + 1}{x^4}\right)^n + c$, we get:

$m = -\dfrac{2}{5}$ and $n = \dfrac{5}{8}$

Therefore, the value of $\dfrac{n}{m}$ is:

$\dfrac{n}{m} = \dfrac{5/8}{-2/5} = \dfrac{5}{8} \times \left(-\dfrac{5}{2}\right) = -\dfrac{25}{16}$

Answer: $-\dfrac{25}{16}$

questions.q: If $f(x) = \dfrac{1}{\log x}$ and $g(x) = \dfrac{1}{(\log x)^2}$, then the value of $\displaystyle\int [f(x) - g(x)]\,dx$ is...
questions.solution:
Let $I = \int \left( \dfrac{1}{\log x} - \dfrac{1}{(\log x)^2} \right) dx$

Substitute $\log x = t \Rightarrow x = e^t \Rightarrow dx = e^t dt$

$I = \int e^t \left( \dfrac{1}{t} - \dfrac{1}{t^2} \right) dt$

Using the standard integral $\int e^t (h(t) + h'(t)) dt = e^t h(t) + c$

Here, $h(t) = \dfrac{1}{t}$ and $h'(t) = -\dfrac{1}{t^2}$

$I = e^t \left( \dfrac{1}{t} \right) + c$

Substituting back $t = \log x$ and $e^t = x$

$I = \dfrac{x}{\log x} + c$

Answer: $\dfrac{x}{\log x} + c$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The value of integral $\displaystyle\int \dfrac{\sqrt{x^2 + 1}\,[\log(x^2 + 1) - 2\log x]}{x^4}\,dx$ is equal to...
questions.solution:
Let the given integral be $I = \int \dfrac{\sqrt{x^2+1} [\log(x^2+1) - 2\log x]}{x^4} dx$

$I = \int \dfrac{\sqrt{x^2(1+\dfrac{1}{x^2})}}{x^4} [\log(x^2+1) - \log x^2] dx$

$I = \int \dfrac{x\sqrt{1+\dfrac{1}{x^2}}}{x^4} \log\left(\dfrac{x^2+1}{x^2}\right) dx$

$I = \int \dfrac{1}{x^3}\sqrt{1+\dfrac{1}{x^2}} \log\left(1+\dfrac{1}{x^2}\right) dx$

Substituting $1+\dfrac{1}{x^2} = t$

Differentiating with respect to $x$, we get $-\dfrac{2}{x^3} dx = dt \Rightarrow \dfrac{1}{x^3} dx = -\dfrac{1}{2} dt$

$I = \int \sqrt{t} \log t \left(-\dfrac{1}{2}\right) dt$

$I = -\dfrac{1}{2} \int t^{1/2} \log t dt$

Using integration by parts, taking $\log t$ as the first function and $t^{1/2}$ as the second function:

$I = -\dfrac{1}{2} \left[ \log t \int t^{1/2} dt - \int \left( \dfrac{d}{dt}(\log t) \int t^{1/2} dt \right) dt \right]$

$I = -\dfrac{1}{2} \left[ \log t \left(\dfrac{t^{3/2}}{3/2}\right) - \int \dfrac{1}{t} \left(\dfrac{t^{3/2}}{3/2}\right) dt \right]$

$I = -\dfrac{1}{2} \left[ \dfrac{2}{3} t^{3/2} \log t - \dfrac{2}{3} \int t^{1/2} dt \right]$

$I = -\dfrac{1}{2} \left[ \dfrac{2}{3} t^{3/2} \log t - \dfrac{2}{3} \left(\dfrac{t^{3/2}}{3/2}\right) \right] + c$

$I = -\dfrac{1}{2} \left[ \dfrac{2}{3} t^{3/2} \log t - \dfrac{4}{9} t^{3/2} \right] + c$

$I = t^{3/2} \left[ -\dfrac{1}{3} \log t + \dfrac{2}{9} \right] + c$

Substituting $t = 1+\dfrac{1}{x^2}$ back into the expression:

$I = \left(1+\dfrac{1}{x^2}\right)^{3/2} \left[ -\dfrac{1}{3} \log\left(1+\dfrac{1}{x^2}\right) + \dfrac{2}{9} \right] + c$

questions.q: The value of integral $\displaystyle\int \dfrac{dx}{\sin^2 x + \tan^2 x}$ is...
questions.solution:
Given integral is $I = \displaystyle\int \dfrac{dx}{\sin^2 x + \tan^2 x}$

Rewriting the denominator:

$\sin^2 x + \tan^2 x = \sin^2 x + \dfrac{\sin^2 x}{\cos^2 x} = \sin^2 x \left( \dfrac{\cos^2 x + 1}{\cos^2 x} \right) = \tan^2 x (\cos^2 x + 1)$

Substituting this back into the integral:

$I = \displaystyle\int \dfrac{dx}{\tan^2 x (\cos^2 x + 1)}$

Multiplying the numerator and the denominator by $\sec^2 x$:

$I = \displaystyle\int \dfrac{\sec^2 x}{\tan^2 x (\cos^2 x + 1) \sec^2 x} dx$

$I = \displaystyle\int \dfrac{\sec^2 x}{\tan^2 x (1 + \sec^2 x)} dx$

Using the identity $\sec^2 x = 1 + \tan^2 x$:

$I = \displaystyle\int \dfrac{\sec^2 x}{\tan^2 x (2 + \tan^2 x)} dx$

Let $\tan x = t$, then $\sec^2 x dx = dt$. The integral becomes:

$I = \displaystyle\int \dfrac{dt}{t^2 (t^2 + 2)}$

Using partial fractions:

$\dfrac{1}{t^2 (t^2 + 2)} = \dfrac{1}{2} \left( \dfrac{1}{t^2} - \dfrac{1}{t^2 + 2} \right)$

$I = \dfrac{1}{2} \displaystyle\int \left( \dfrac{1}{t^2} - \dfrac{1}{t^2 + (\sqrt{2})^2} \right) dt$

Integrating with respect to $t$:

$I = \dfrac{1}{2} \left( -\dfrac{1}{t} - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \tan^{-1} \left( \dfrac{t}{\sqrt{2}} \right) \right) + c$

$I = \dfrac{-1}{2t} - \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{2}} \tan^{-1} \left( \dfrac{t}{\sqrt{2}} \right) + c$

Substituting $t = \tan x$ back into the expression:

$I = \dfrac{-1}{2\tan x} - \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{2}} \tan^{-1} \left( \dfrac{\tan x}{\sqrt{2}} \right) + c$

Answer: $\dfrac{-1}{2\tan x} - \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{\tan x}{\sqrt{2}}\right) + c$

questions.q: If $\sin^{-1}\left(\tan\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) - \sin^{-1}\left(\sqrt{\dfrac{3}{x}}\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$ then $x$ is a root of the equation
questions.solution:
Given equation is $\sin^{-1}\left(\tan\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) - \sin^{-1}\left(\sqrt{\dfrac{3}{x}}\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$

Since $\tan\dfrac{\pi}{4} = 1$, we have:

$\sin^{-1}(1) - \sin^{-1}\left(\sqrt{\dfrac{3}{x}}\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$

$\dfrac{\pi}{2} - \sin^{-1}\left(\sqrt{\dfrac{3}{x}}\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{6}$

$\sin^{-1}\left(\sqrt{\dfrac{3}{x}}\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{2} - \dfrac{\pi}{6} = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$

$\sqrt{\dfrac{3}{x}} = \sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$

Squaring both sides, we get:

$\dfrac{3}{x} = \dfrac{3}{4}$

$x = 4$

Substituting $x = 4$ into the given options, we find that it satisfies the equation $x^2 - x - 12 = 0$ since $4^2 - 4 - 12 = 16 - 16 = 0$.

Answer: $x^2 - x - 12 = 0$

questions.q: $\sum\limits_{k=1}^{2026} \sin^{-1}\left(\cos\dfrac{k\pi}{4}\right) =$
questions.solution:
Let $f(k) = \sin^{-1}\left(\cos\dfrac{k\pi}{4}\right)$.

The function $\cos\dfrac{k\pi}{4}$ is periodic with a period of $8$.

Let us evaluate the sum of $f(k)$ over one complete period, from $k=1$ to $k=8$:

$f(1) = \sin^{-1}\left(\cos\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = \sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$

$f(2) = \sin^{-1}\left(\cos\dfrac{2\pi}{4}\right) = \sin^{-1}(0) = 0$

$f(3) = \sin^{-1}\left(\cos\dfrac{3\pi}{4}\right) = \sin^{-1}\left(-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right) = -\dfrac{\pi}{4}$

$f(4) = \sin^{-1}\left(\cos\dfrac{4\pi}{4}\right) = \sin^{-1}(-1) = -\dfrac{\pi}{2}$

$f(5) = \sin^{-1}\left(\cos\dfrac{5\pi}{4}\right) = \sin^{-1}\left(-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right) = -\dfrac{\pi}{4}$

$f(6) = \sin^{-1}\left(\cos\dfrac{6\pi}{4}\right) = \sin^{-1}(0) = 0$

$f(7) = \sin^{-1}\left(\cos\dfrac{7\pi}{4}\right) = \sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right) = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$

$f(8) = \sin^{-1}\left(\cos\dfrac{8\pi}{4}\right) = \sin^{-1}(1) = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$

Summing these values, we get:

$\sum\limits_{k=1}^{8} f(k) = \dfrac{\pi}{4} + 0 - \dfrac{\pi}{4} - \dfrac{\pi}{2} - \dfrac{\pi}{4} + 0 + \dfrac{\pi}{4} + \dfrac{\pi}{2} = 0$

Since the sum over any $8$ consecutive terms is $0$, we divide the total number of terms by $8$:

$2026 = 8 \times 253 + 2$

This means there are $253$ complete periods whose sum is $0$, leaving only the first $2$ terms of the next period.

$\sum\limits_{k=1}^{2026} f(k) = 253 \times 0 + f(1) + f(2)$

$\sum\limits_{k=1}^{2026} f(k) = \dfrac{\pi}{4} + 0 = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$

Answer: $\dfrac{\pi}{4}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The value of $\lim\limits_{x \to 0}\left(\dfrac{8}{x^8}\right)\left[1 - \cos\dfrac{x^2}{2} - \cos\dfrac{x^2}{4} + \cos\dfrac{x^2}{2}\cdot\cos\dfrac{x^2}{4}\right]$ is equal to ...
questions.solution:
The given expression inside the limit can be factored as:

$\left(1 - \cos\dfrac{x^2}{2}\right)\left(1 - \cos\dfrac{x^2}{4}\right)$

The limit becomes:

$\lim\limits_{x \to 0} \dfrac{8}{x^8} \left(1 - \cos\dfrac{x^2}{2}\right)\left(1 - \cos\dfrac{x^2}{4}\right)$

Using the standard limit $\lim\limits_{\theta \to 0} \dfrac{1 - \cos \theta}{\theta^2} = \dfrac{1}{2}$, we can rewrite the expression as:

$\lim\limits_{x \to 0} \dfrac{8}{x^8} \left( \dfrac{1 - \cos\dfrac{x^2}{2}}{\left(\dfrac{x^2}{2}\right)^2} \cdot \dfrac{x^4}{4} \right) \left( \dfrac{1 - \cos\dfrac{x^2}{4}}{\left(\dfrac{x^2}{4}\right)^2} \cdot \dfrac{x^4}{16} \right)$

Evaluating the standard limits:

$= \lim\limits_{x \to 0} \dfrac{8}{x^8} \left( \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot \dfrac{x^4}{4} \right) \left( \dfrac{1}{2} \cdot \dfrac{x^4}{16} \right)$

$= \lim\limits_{x \to 0} \dfrac{8}{x^8} \left( \dfrac{x^4}{8} \right) \left( \dfrac{x^4}{32} \right)$

$= \lim\limits_{x \to 0} \dfrac{8}{x^8} \cdot \dfrac{x^8}{256}$

$= \dfrac{8}{256} = \dfrac{1}{32}$

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{32}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If the function $f(x) = \dfrac{2\sqrt{2} - (\cos x + \sin x)^3}{1 - \sin 2x}$ is continuous at $x = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$, then the value of $f\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$ is ...
questions.solution:
Since $f(x)$ is continuous at $x = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$, we have $f\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = \lim_{x \to \pi/4} f(x)$.

Let $t = \cos x + \sin x$. As $x \to \dfrac{\pi}{4}$, $t \to \cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) + \sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = \sqrt{2}$.

Squaring both sides, $t^2 = (\cos x + \sin x)^2 = \cos^2 x + \sin^2 x + 2\sin x \cos x = 1 + \sin 2x$.

This gives $\sin 2x = t^2 - 1$.

Substituting these into the limit:

$\lim_{x \to \pi/4} \dfrac{2\sqrt{2} - (\cos x + \sin x)^3}{1 - \sin 2x} = \lim_{t \to \sqrt{2}} \dfrac{2\sqrt{2} - t^3}{1 - (t^2 - 1)} = \lim_{t \to \sqrt{2}} \dfrac{2\sqrt{2} - t^3}{2 - t^2}$

This is a $\dfrac{0}{0}$ form. Applying L'Hopital's rule:

$\lim_{t \to \sqrt{2}} \dfrac{-3t^2}{-2t} = \lim_{t \to \sqrt{2}} \dfrac{3t}{2} = \dfrac{3\sqrt{2}}{2}$

Alternatively, by factorizing:

$\lim_{t \to \sqrt{2}} \dfrac{(\sqrt{2} - t)(2 + \sqrt{2}t + t^2)}{(\sqrt{2} - t)(\sqrt{2} + t)} = \lim_{t \to \sqrt{2}} \dfrac{2 + \sqrt{2}t + t^2}{\sqrt{2} + t} = \dfrac{2 + 2 + 2}{\sqrt{2} + \sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{6}{2\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{3\sqrt{2}}{2}$

Thus, $f\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = \dfrac{3\sqrt{2}}{2}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{3\sqrt{2}}{2}$

questions.q: The shaded region in the provided graph represents the solution set for which of the following systems of linear inequalities?
options: $2x + y \geq 2,\ x - y \geq 1,\ x + 2y \leq 8,\ x \geq 0,\ y \geq 0$
$2x + y \geq 2,\ x - y \leq 1,\ x + 2y \leq 8,\ x \geq 0,\ y \geq 0$
$2x + y \geq 2,\ x - y \leq 1,\ 2x + y \leq 8,\ x \geq 0,\ y \geq 0$
questions.solution:
The equations of the lines forming the boundaries of the shaded region are determined as follows.

The line passing through the points $E(0, 2)$ and $A(1, 0)$ has the equation $\dfrac{x}{1} + \dfrac{y}{2} = 1$, which simplifies to $2x + y = 2$. The shaded region lies away from the origin relative to this line. Testing a point inside the region, such as $(1, 2)$, gives $2(1) + 2 = 4 \geq 2$. Thus, the corresponding inequality is $2x + y \geq 2$.

The line passing through the points $D(0, 4)$ and $B\left(\dfrac{10}{3}, \dfrac{7}{3}\right)$ has a slope $m = \dfrac{\dfrac{7}{3} - 4}{\dfrac{10}{3} - 0} = -\dfrac{1}{2}$. Its equation is $y - 4 = -\dfrac{1}{2}(x - 0)$, which simplifies to $x + 2y = 8$. The shaded region lies towards the origin relative to this line. Testing the point $(1, 2)$ gives $1 + 2(2) = 5 \leq 8$. Thus, the corresponding inequality is $x + 2y \leq 8$.

The line passing through the points $A(1, 0)$ and $B\left(\dfrac{10}{3}, \dfrac{7}{3}\right)$ has a slope $m = \dfrac{\dfrac{7}{3} - 0}{\dfrac{10}{3} - 1} = 1$. Its equation is $y - 0 = 1(x - 1)$, which simplifies to $x - y = 1$. The shaded region lies towards the origin relative to this line. Testing the point $(1, 2)$ gives $1 - 2 = -1 \leq 1$. Thus, the corresponding inequality is $x - y \leq 1$.

The shaded region is bounded by the y-axis on the left, which means $x \geq 0$. It also lies entirely in the first quadrant, so $y \geq 0$.

Combining all these conditions, the system of linear inequalities is $2x + y \geq 2$, $x - y \leq 1$, $x + 2y \leq 8$, $x \geq 0$, $y \geq 0$.

Answer: $2x + y \geq 2,\ x - y \leq 1,\ x + 2y \leq 8,\ x \geq 0,\ y \geq 0$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Which of the following logical statements is a tautology?
questions.solution:
Consider the first option: $[(p \rightarrow q) \wedge \sim q] \rightarrow \sim p$

Using logical equivalences, we know that $p \rightarrow q \equiv \sim p \vee q$.

Substituting this into the premise:
$(p \rightarrow q) \wedge \sim q \equiv (\sim p \vee q) \wedge \sim q$
$\equiv (\sim p \wedge \sim q) \vee (q \wedge \sim q)$
$\equiv (\sim p \wedge \sim q) \vee F$
$\equiv \sim p \wedge \sim q$

Now, substituting this back into the original statement:
$(\sim p \wedge \sim q) \rightarrow \sim p$
$\equiv \sim(\sim p \wedge \sim q) \vee \sim p$
$\equiv (p \vee q) \vee \sim p$
$\equiv (p \vee \sim p) \vee q$
$\equiv T \vee q \equiv T$

Since the final truth value is always True ($T$), this statement is a tautology.

Checking the other options for completeness:
$(p \rightarrow q) \wedge (p \wedge \sim q) \equiv (\sim p \vee q) \wedge \sim(\sim p \vee q) \equiv F$ (Contradiction)

$[(p \vee q) \wedge \sim p] \wedge \sim q \equiv (q \wedge \sim p) \wedge \sim q \equiv \sim p \wedge (q \wedge \sim q) \equiv F$ (Contradiction)

$[(p \vee \sim q) \vee (\sim p \wedge q)] \wedge r \equiv [(p \vee \sim q \vee \sim p) \wedge (p \vee \sim q \vee q)] \wedge r \equiv (T \wedge T) \wedge r \equiv r$ (Not a tautology)

Answer: $[(p \rightarrow q) \wedge \sim q] \rightarrow \sim p$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The logical statement $(p \vee q) \wedge [(\sim p \wedge q) \vee (p \wedge \sim q)] \wedge \sim q$ is logically equivalent to ...
questions.solution:
Given statement: $(p \vee q) \wedge [(\sim p \wedge q) \vee (p \wedge \sim q)] \wedge \sim q$

Consider the part $[(\sim p \wedge q) \vee (p \wedge \sim q)] \wedge \sim q$

Using distributive law:

$= ((\sim p \wedge q) \wedge \sim q) \vee ((p \wedge \sim q) \wedge \sim q)$

$= (\sim p \wedge (q \wedge \sim q)) \vee (p \wedge (\sim q \wedge \sim q))$

$= (\sim p \wedge F) \vee (p \wedge \sim q)$

$= F \vee (p \wedge \sim q)$

$= p \wedge \sim q$

Now, substitute this back into the original statement:

$= (p \vee q) \wedge (p \wedge \sim q)$

Using distributive law:

$= (p \wedge (p \wedge \sim q)) \vee (q \wedge (p \wedge \sim q))$

$= ((p \wedge p) \wedge \sim q) \vee (p \wedge (q \wedge \sim q))$

$= (p \wedge \sim q) \vee (p \wedge F)$

$= (p \wedge \sim q) \vee F$

$= p \wedge \sim q$

Answer: $p \wedge \sim q$
