questions.q: The inverse of matrix $\begin{bmatrix} 1+pq & p & 0 \\ q & 1+pq & p \\ 0 & q & 1 \end{bmatrix}$ is ...
options: $\begin{bmatrix} 1 & p & p^2 \\ q & 1+pq & p+p^2q \\ q^2 & q+pq^2 & 1+pq+p^2q^2 \end{bmatrix}$
questions.solution:
Let the given matrix be $A = \begin{bmatrix} 1+pq & p & 0 \\ q & 1+pq & p \\ 0 & q & 1 \end{bmatrix}$.

The inverse of matrix $A$ is given by $A^{-1} = \dfrac{1}{|A|}\text{adj}(A)$.

First, evaluate the determinant of $A$:

$|A| = (1+pq)[(1+pq)(1) - (p)(q)] - p[q(1) - (p)(0)] + 0$

$|A| = (1+pq)[1 + pq - pq] - p[q]$

$|A| = (1+pq)(1) - pq = 1 + pq - pq = 1$

Since $|A| = 1$, the inverse matrix is $A^{-1} = \text{adj}(A)$.

To find the adjoint of $A$, we calculate the cofactors of each element:

$C_{11} = (1+pq)(1) - pq = 1$

$C_{12} = -(q(1) - 0) = -q$

$C_{13} = q(q) - 0 = q^2$

$C_{21} = -(p(1) - 0) = -p$

$C_{22} = (1+pq)(1) - 0 = 1+pq$

$C_{23} = -((1+pq)q - 0) = -(q + pq^2)$

$C_{31} = p(p) - 0 = p^2$

$C_{32} = -((1+pq)p - 0) = -(p + p^2q)$

$C_{33} = (1+pq)^2 - pq = 1 + 2pq + p^2q^2 - pq = 1 + pq + p^2q^2$

The adjoint matrix is the transpose of the cofactor matrix:

$\text{adj}(A) = \begin{bmatrix} C_{11} & C_{21} & C_{31} \\ C_{12} & C_{22} & C_{32} \\ C_{13} & C_{23} & C_{33} \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -p & p^2 \\ -q & 1+pq & -(p+p^2q) \\ q^2 & -(q+pq^2) & 1+pq+p^2q^2 \end{bmatrix}$

Therefore, $A^{-1} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -p & p^2 \\ -q & 1+pq & -(p+p^2q) \\ q^2 & -(q+pq^2) & 1+pq+p^2q^2 \end{bmatrix}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $A = [a_{ij}]_{3\times3}$, where $a_{ij} = \begin{cases} 1, & \text{if } i+j \text{ is even} \\ 0, & \text{if } i+j \text{ is odd} \end{cases}$, then $\text{adj}(A) = \ldots$ ..
questions.solution:
Given $A = [a_{ij}]_{3\times3}$ where $a_{ij} = 1$ if $i+j$ is even, and $0$ if $i+j$ is odd.

Constructing the matrix $A$:

$A = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 1 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$

The adjoint of $A$ is the transpose of the cofactor matrix $C$. Calculating the cofactors $C_{ij} = (-1)^{i+j} M_{ij}$:

$C_{11} = 1, C_{12} = 0, C_{13} = -1$

$C_{21} = 0, C_{22} = 0, C_{23} = 0$

$C_{31} = -1, C_{32} = 0, C_{33} = 1$

The cofactor matrix is $C = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$.

Taking the transpose of $C$ gives the adjoint matrix:

$\text{adj}(A) = C^T = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$

Answer: $\begin{bmatrix} 1 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ -1 & 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If the combined equation of angle bisectors of the lines $x^2 - 2pxy - y^2 = 0$ is $x^2 - 2qxy - y^2 = 0$, then which of the following is true?
questions.solution:
The given equation of the pair of lines is $x^2 - 2pxy - y^2 = 0$.

Comparing this with the standard equation $ax^2 + 2hxy + by^2 = 0$, we get $a = 1$, $h = -p$, and $b = -1$.

The combined equation of the angle bisectors is given by the formula $\dfrac{x^2 - y^2}{a - b} = \dfrac{xy}{h}$.

Substituting the values of $a$, $h$, and $b$, we get:

$\dfrac{x^2 - y^2}{1 - (-1)} = \dfrac{xy}{-p}$

$\dfrac{x^2 - y^2}{2} = \dfrac{xy}{-p}$

$-p(x^2 - y^2) = 2xy$

$px^2 + 2xy - py^2 = 0$

Dividing the entire equation by $p$, we obtain:

$x^2 + \dfrac{2}{p}xy - y^2 = 0$

It is given that the combined equation of the angle bisectors is $x^2 - 2qxy - y^2 = 0$.

Comparing the coefficients of $xy$ in both equations, we get:

$-2q = \dfrac{2}{p}$

$-q = \dfrac{1}{p}$

$pq = -1$

$pq + 1 = 0$

Answer: $pq + 1 = 0$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Four men and three women are to be arranged at a round table. The number of arrangements in which no two women are together is ....
questions.solution:
First, arrange the $4$ men around the circular table. The number of ways to do this is $(4 - 1)! = 3!$.

When the $4$ men are seated, they create $4$ gaps between them.

To ensure that no two women sit together, the $3$ women must be placed in these $4$ gaps.

The number of ways to choose $3$ gaps out of $4$ and arrange the $3$ women in them is $^{4}P_{3} = 4 \times 3 \times 2 = 4!$.

Therefore, the total number of arrangements is $3! \times 4!$.

Answer: $3! \times 4!$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Consider a game of tossing a six sided fair die. If the face that comes up is $6$, the player wins Rs. $36$ and he loses Rs. $k^2$, where $k$ is the face that comes up $k = \{1, 2, 3, 4, 5\}$, then the expected winning amount in this game in Rs. is...
questions.solution:
Let $X$ be the random variable representing the winning amount.

The possible values of $X$ corresponding to the outcomes $1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6$ on the die are $-1^2, -2^2, -3^2, -4^2, -5^2, 36$ respectively, which simplifies to $-1, -4, -9, -16, -25, 36$.

Since the die is fair, the probability of each outcome is $\dfrac{1}{6}$.

The expected winning amount is given by $E(X) = \sum x_i P(x_i)$.

$E(X) = \dfrac{1}{6}(-1) + \dfrac{1}{6}(-4) + \dfrac{1}{6}(-9) + \dfrac{1}{6}(-16) + \dfrac{1}{6}(-25) + \dfrac{1}{6}(36)$

$E(X) = \dfrac{1}{6}(-1 - 4 - 9 - 16 - 25 + 36)$

$E(X) = \dfrac{1}{6}(-55 + 36)$

$E(X) = -\dfrac{19}{6}$

Answer: $-\dfrac{19}{6}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q:
Given the probability density function (p.d.f.) of the random variable X, $f(x) = \dfrac{1}{2a}$, $0 \lt x \lt 2a$, $a \gt 0$
$= 0$, otherwise, then which of the following is correct ?
questions.solution:
The given probability density function is $f(x) = \dfrac{1}{2a}$ for $0 \lt x \lt 2a$, and $0$ otherwise.

We calculate the probability $P\left(X \lt \dfrac{a}{2}\right)$:

$P\left(X \lt \dfrac{a}{2}\right) = \int_{0}^{\dfrac{a}{2}} f(x) dx = \int_{0}^{\dfrac{a}{2}} \dfrac{1}{2a} dx = \dfrac{1}{2a} [x]_{0}^{\dfrac{a}{2}} = \dfrac{1}{2a} \left(\dfrac{a}{2} - 0\right) = \dfrac{1}{4}$

Next, we calculate the probability $P\left(X \gt \dfrac{3a}{2}\right)$:

$P\left(X \gt \dfrac{3a}{2}\right) = \int_{\dfrac{3a}{2}}^{2a} f(x) dx = \int_{\dfrac{3a}{2}}^{2a} \dfrac{1}{2a} dx = \dfrac{1}{2a} [x]_{\dfrac{3a}{2}}^{2a} = \dfrac{1}{2a} \left(2a - \dfrac{3a}{2}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2a} \left(\dfrac{a}{2}\right) = \dfrac{1}{4}$

Comparing the two probabilities, we get:

$P\left(X \lt \dfrac{a}{2}\right) = P\left(X \gt \dfrac{3a}{2}\right) = \dfrac{1}{4}$

Answer: $P\left(X \lt \dfrac{a}{2}\right) = P\left(X \gt \dfrac{3a}{2}\right)$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If in $6$ trials, X is a binomial random variable which follows the relation $9P(x = 4) = P(x = 2)$, then the probability of failure is...
questions.solution:
Let $p$ be the probability of success and $q$ be the probability of failure in a single trial, where $p + q = 1$.

For a binomial distribution with $n = 6$ trials, the probability of $x$ successes is given by $P(X = x) = ^{6}C_{x} p^{x} q^{6-x}$.

Given the relation:

$9P(X = 4) = P(X = 2)$

Substituting the binomial probabilities:

$9 \times ^{6}C_{4} p^{4} q^{2} = ^{6}C_{2} p^{2} q^{4}$

Since $^{6}C_{4} = ^{6}C_{2} = 15$, we can cancel it from both sides:

$9 p^{4} q^{2} = p^{2} q^{4}$

Dividing both sides by $p^{2} q^{2}$ (assuming $p, q \neq 0$):

$9 p^{2} = q^{2}$

Taking the square root on both sides (since probabilities are non-negative):

$3p = q$

We know that $p + q = 1$. Substituting $p = \dfrac{q}{3}$:

$\dfrac{q}{3} + q = 1$

$\dfrac{4q}{3} = 1$

$q = \dfrac{3}{4} = 0.75$

Thus, the probability of failure is $0.75$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: In $\triangle ABC$, with usual notations, if the sides $a$, $b$ and $c$ are in the ratio $18 : 17 : 7$, then $\cot\dfrac{A}{2} : \cot\dfrac{B}{2} : \cot\dfrac{C}{2} =$
questions.solution:
Let the sides of the triangle be $a = 18k$, $b = 17k$, and $c = 7k$.

The semi-perimeter $s$ is given by:

$s = \dfrac{a+b+c}{2} = \dfrac{18k + 17k + 7k}{2} = 21k$

Using the half-angle formula for cotangent:

$\cot\dfrac{A}{2} = \sqrt{\dfrac{s(s-a)}{(s-b)(s-c)}} = \dfrac{s(s-a)}{\Delta}$

Similarly, $\cot\dfrac{B}{2} = \dfrac{s(s-b)}{\Delta}$ and $\cot\dfrac{C}{2} = \dfrac{s(s-c)}{\Delta}$.

Thus, the required ratio is:

$\cot\dfrac{A}{2} : \cot\dfrac{B}{2} : \cot\dfrac{C}{2} = (s-a) : (s-b) : (s-c)$

Substituting the values of $s$, $a$, $b$, and $c$:

$s-a = 21k - 18k = 3k$

$s-b = 21k - 17k = 4k$

$s-c = 21k - 7k = 14k$

Therefore, the ratio is:

$3k : 4k : 14k = 3 : 4 : 14$

Answer: $3 : 4 : 14$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Let $a$ be an integer selected at random from the set $\{0, 1, 2, 3, \ldots, 9\}$. The probability that the equation $ax^2 - ax + 1 = 0$ has real roots is ...
questions.solution:
The total number of possible values for $a$ from the set $\{0, 1, 2, 3, \ldots, 9\}$ is $10$.

For the equation $ax^2 - ax + 1 = 0$ to have real roots, we consider two cases:

If $a = 0$, the equation becomes $1 = 0$, which has no roots.

If $a \neq 0$, the equation is a quadratic equation. For it to have real roots, its discriminant must be non-negative.

$D = (-a)^2 - 4(a)(1) \geq 0$

$a^2 - 4a \geq 0$

$a(a - 4) \geq 0$

Since $a \in \{1, 2, 3, \ldots, 9\}$, the condition $a(a - 4) \geq 0$ is satisfied when $a \geq 4$.

The favorable values of $a$ are $4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9$.

The number of favorable outcomes is $6$.

The required probability is $\dfrac{6}{10} = \dfrac{3}{5}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{3}{5}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A straight line L passes through the point of intersection of the lines $x - y + 1 = 0$ and $2x + y - 7 = 0$. If L intersects the positive x-axis at $A(a, 0)$ and the positive y-axis at $B(0, b)$, then the minimum area of the triangle $OAB$ (where $O$ is the origin) is ....
questions.solution:
Solving the equations $x - y + 1 = 0$ and $2x + y - 7 = 0$, we get the point of intersection as $(2, 3)$.

Let the equation of the line $L$ be $\dfrac{x}{a} + \dfrac{y}{b} = 1$.

Since it passes through $(2, 3)$, we have:

$\dfrac{2}{a} + \dfrac{3}{b} = 1$

Since $L$ intersects the positive x-axis and positive y-axis, $a \gt 0$ and $b \gt 0$. Applying the AM-GM inequality on $\dfrac{2}{a}$ and $\dfrac{3}{b}$:

$\dfrac{\dfrac{2}{a} + \dfrac{3}{b}}{2} \ge \sqrt{\dfrac{2}{a} \times \dfrac{3}{b}}$

$\dfrac{1}{2} \ge \sqrt{\dfrac{6}{ab}}$

Squaring both sides:

$\dfrac{1}{4} \ge \dfrac{6}{ab} \Rightarrow ab \ge 24$

The area of the triangle $OAB$ is given by $\Delta = \dfrac{1}{2}ab$.

$\Delta \ge \dfrac{1}{2} \times 24 = 12$

The minimum area of the triangle is $12$ square units.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: A line making equal intercepts on coordinate axes and is tangent to the circle $x^2 + y^2 = 4$. The length of each intercept made by line on the coordinate axes is ...
questions.solution:
Let the equation of the line making equal intercepts on the coordinate axes be $\dfrac{x}{a} + \dfrac{y}{a} = 1$.

This can be written as $x + y - a = 0$.

The line is tangent to the circle $x^2 + y^2 = 4$.

The center of the circle is $(0, 0)$ and its radius is $2$.

For a line to be tangent to a circle, the perpendicular distance from the center of the circle to the line must be equal to the radius.

$\dfrac{|0 + 0 - a|}{\sqrt{1^2 + 1^2}} = 2$

$\dfrac{|a|}{\sqrt{2}} = 2$

$|a| = 2\sqrt{2}$

The length of each intercept made by the line on the coordinate axes is $2\sqrt{2}$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The symmetric form of the equation of the line $x = ay + b$, $z = cy + d$ is
questions.solution:
Given equations of the line are $x = ay + b$ and $z = cy + d$.

From the first equation, expressing $y$ in terms of $x$:

$x - b = ay \Rightarrow y = \dfrac{x - b}{a}$

From the second equation, expressing $y$ in terms of $z$:

$z - d = cy \Rightarrow y = \dfrac{z - d}{c}$

Equating the expressions for $y$, the symmetric form of the line is:

$\dfrac{x - b}{a} = y = \dfrac{z - d}{c}$

Answer: $\dfrac{x - b}{a} = y = \dfrac{z - d}{c}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $p$ is the shortest distance between the lines $\dfrac{x+1}{7} = \dfrac{y+1}{-6} = z+1$ and $\vec{r} = (3\hat{i} + 5\hat{j} + 7\hat{k}) + \mu(\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + \hat{k})$ then $[p]$ is... ,(where $[\,.\,]$ denotes the greatest integer function.)
questions.solution:
The shortest distance $p$ between two lines $\vec{r} = \vec{a}_1 + \lambda \vec{b}_1$ and $\vec{r} = \vec{a}_2 + \mu \vec{b}_2$ is given by $p = \dfrac{|(\vec{a}_2 - \vec{a}_1) \cdot (\vec{b}_1 \times \vec{b}_2)|}{|\vec{b}_1 \times \vec{b}_2|}$.

For the first line, $\vec{a}_1 = -\hat{i} - \hat{j} - \hat{k}$ and $\vec{b}_1 = 7\hat{i} - 6\hat{j} + \hat{k}$.

For the second line, $\vec{a}_2 = 3\hat{i} + 5\hat{j} + 7\hat{k}$ and $\vec{b}_2 = \hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + \hat{k}$.

$\vec{a}_2 - \vec{a}_1 = 4\hat{i} + 6\hat{j} + 8\hat{k}$

$\vec{b}_1 \times \vec{b}_2 = \begin{vmatrix} \hat{i} & \hat{j} & \hat{k} \\ 7 & -6 & 1 \\ 1 & -2 & 1 \end{vmatrix} = -4\hat{i} - 6\hat{j} - 8\hat{k}$

$(\vec{a}_2 - \vec{a}_1) \cdot (\vec{b}_1 \times \vec{b}_2) = (4)(-4) + (6)(-6) + (8)(-8) = -16 - 36 - 64 = -116$

$|\vec{b}_1 \times \vec{b}_2| = \sqrt{(-4)^2 + (-6)^2 + (-8)^2} = \sqrt{16 + 36 + 64} = \sqrt{116}$

$p = \dfrac{|-116|}{\sqrt{116}} = \sqrt{116}$

Since $100 \lt 116 \lt 121$, we have $10 \lt \sqrt{116} \lt 11$.

Therefore, $[p] = 10$.

Answer: $10$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: From a point P $(a, b, c)$, perpendiculars PA and PB are drawn to XY plane and ZX plane respectively. If O is the origin, then the equation of plane OAB is
questions.solution:
The coordinates of point P are $(a, b, c)$.

Since PA is perpendicular to the XY plane, the $z$-coordinate of A is $0$. Thus, the coordinates of A are $(a, b, 0)$.

Since PB is perpendicular to the ZX plane, the $y$-coordinate of B is $0$. Thus, the coordinates of B are $(a, 0, c)$.

The equation of the plane passing through the origin O $(0, 0, 0)$, A $(a, b, 0)$, and B $(a, 0, c)$ is given by:

$\begin{vmatrix} x & y & z \\ a & b & 0 \\ a & 0 & c \end{vmatrix} = 0$

Expanding the determinant along the first row, we get:

$x(bc - 0) - y(ac - 0) + z(0 - ab) = 0$

$bcx - acy - abz = 0$

Dividing the entire equation by $abc$, we get:

$\dfrac{x}{a} - \dfrac{y}{b} - \dfrac{z}{c} = 0$

Answer: $\dfrac{x}{a} - \dfrac{y}{b} - \dfrac{z}{c} = 0$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The plane $\dfrac{x}{2} + \dfrac{y}{3} + \dfrac{z}{4} = 1$ cuts the axes at the points A, B, C then the area of triangle ABC is
questions.solution:
\Delta ABC$ is given by $\Delta = \sqrt{\Delta_{xy}^2 + \Delta_{yz}^2 + \Delta_{zx}^2}$, where $\Delta_{xy}$, $\Delta_{yz}$, and $\Delta_{zx}$ are the areas of the projections of $\Delta ABC$ on the $xy$, $yz$, and $zx$ planes respectively.

$\Delta_{xy} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 2 \times 3 = 3$

$\Delta_{yz} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 3 \times 4 = 6$

$\Delta_{zx} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 4 \times 2 = 4$

$\Delta = \sqrt{3^2 + 6^2 + 4^2} = \sqrt{9 + 36 + 16} = \sqrt{61}$

Answer: $\sqrt{61}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: Let $x \in [0, 6\pi]$ satisfy the equation $\cos x - \sin x = -1$. If $x = k\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)$ where $k \in N$, then find the number of possible values of $k$ is .....
questions.solution:
Given equation: $\cos x - \sin x = -1$

$\Rightarrow \cos x + 1 = \sin x$

Squaring both sides:

$\cos^2 x + 2\cos x + 1 = \sin^2 x$

$\Rightarrow \cos^2 x + 2\cos x + 1 = 1 - \cos^2 x$

$\Rightarrow 2\cos^2 x + 2\cos x = 0$

$\Rightarrow 2\cos x(\cos x + 1) = 0$

$\Rightarrow \cos x = 0$ or $\cos x = -1$

If $\cos x = 0$, substituting in the original equation gives $\sin x = 1$.

$\Rightarrow x = 2n\pi + \dfrac{\pi}{2} = (4n+1)\dfrac{\pi}{2}$

Equating with $x = k\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)$, we get $k\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = (4n+1)\dfrac{\pi}{2} \Rightarrow k = \dfrac{3(4n+1)}{2}$

Since $k \in N$, this yields no integer solutions for $k$.

If $\cos x = -1$, substituting in the original equation gives $\sin x = 0$.

$\Rightarrow x = (2n+1)\pi$

Equating with $x = k\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right)$, we get $k\left(\dfrac{\pi}{3}\right) = (2n+1)\pi \Rightarrow k = 3(2n+1)$

Since $x \in [0, 6\pi]$, the possible values of $x$ are $\pi, 3\pi, 5\pi$.

For $x = \pi$, $k = 3$

For $x = 3\pi$, $k = 9$

For $x = 5\pi$, $k = 15$

All these values of $k$ are natural numbers.

Thus, there are $3$ possible values of $k$.

Answer: $3$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The value of $\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{5}\right)$ is ...
questions.solution:
Let $x = \dfrac{\pi}{5}$.

$5x = \pi \Rightarrow 2x = \pi - 3x$

Taking sine on both sides:

$\sin(2x) = \sin(\pi - 3x)$

$\sin(2x) = \sin(3x)$

$2\sin x \cos x = 3\sin x - 4\sin^3 x$

Since $\sin x \neq 0$, dividing by $\sin x$ gives:

$2\cos x = 3 - 4\sin^2 x$

$2\cos x = 3 - 4(1 - \cos^2 x)$

$4\cos^2 x - 2\cos x - 1 = 0$

Solving the quadratic equation for $\cos x$:

$\cos x = \dfrac{2 \pm \sqrt{4 - 4(4)(-1)}}{2(4)} = \dfrac{2 \pm \sqrt{20}}{8} = \dfrac{1 \pm \sqrt{5}}{4}$

Since $x = \dfrac{\pi}{5}$ lies in the first quadrant, $\cos x \gt 0$.

Therefore, $\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{5}\right) = \dfrac{1 + \sqrt{5}}{4}$

Answer: $\dfrac{1 + \sqrt{5}}{4}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $ABC$ is a right-angled triangle in which $BC$ is the longest side and the position vector of $B$ and $C$ are respectively $3\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + \hat{k}$ and $5\hat{i} + \hat{j} - 3\hat{k}$, then the value of $\overline{AB} \cdot \overline{AC} + \overline{BA} \cdot \overline{BC} + \overline{CA} \cdot \overline{CB}$ is
questions.solution:
Since $ABC$ is a right-angled triangle and $BC$ is the longest side, the right angle must be at $A$.

Therefore, $\overline{AB} \cdot \overline{AC} = 0$.

The given expression is $\overline{AB} \cdot \overline{AC} + \overline{BA} \cdot \overline{BC} + \overline{CA} \cdot \overline{CB}$.

Substituting $\overline{AB} \cdot \overline{AC} = 0$, we get:

$0 + \overline{BA} \cdot (\overline{BA} + \overline{AC}) + \overline{CA} \cdot (\overline{CA} + \overline{AB})$

$= |\overline{BA}|^2 + \overline{BA} \cdot \overline{AC} + |\overline{CA}|^2 + \overline{CA} \cdot \overline{AB}$

Since $\overline{BA} \cdot \overline{AC} = 0$ and $\overline{CA} \cdot \overline{AB} = 0$, the expression simplifies to:

$|\overline{BA}|^2 + |\overline{CA}|^2$

By Pythagoras theorem, $|\overline{BA}|^2 + |\overline{CA}|^2 = |\overline{BC}|^2$.

Given the position vectors of $B$ and $C$:

$\vec{B} = 3\hat{i} - 2\hat{j} + \hat{k}$

$\vec{C} = 5\hat{i} + \hat{j} - 3\hat{k}$

$\overline{BC} = \vec{C} - \vec{B} = (5 - 3)\hat{i} + (1 - (-2))\hat{j} + (-3 - 1)\hat{k} = 2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} - 4\hat{k}$

$|\overline{BC}|^2 = (2)^2 + (3)^2 + (-4)^2 = 4 + 9 + 16 = 29$

Thus, the value of the given expression is $29$.

Answer: $29$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The sum of all real values of $\lambda$ for which the vectors $\vec{a} = \lambda\hat{i} + \hat{j} + \hat{k}$, $\vec{b} = \hat{i} + \lambda\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$, $\vec{c} = 2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} + \lambda\hat{k}$ are coplanar is...
questions.solution:
For the vectors $\vec{a}$, $\vec{b}$, and $\vec{c}$ to be coplanar, their scalar triple product must be zero.

$\begin{vmatrix} \lambda & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & \lambda & 2 \\ 2 & 3 & \lambda \end{vmatrix} = 0$

Expanding the determinant:

$\lambda(\lambda^2 - 6) - 1(\lambda - 4) + 1(3 - 2\lambda) = 0$

$\lambda^3 - 6\lambda - \lambda + 4 + 3 - 2\lambda = 0$

$\lambda^3 - 9\lambda + 7 = 0$

Let $f(\lambda) = \lambda^3 - 9\lambda + 7$.

$f'(\lambda) = 3\lambda^2 - 9 = 0 \Rightarrow \lambda = \pm \sqrt{3}$

$f(\sqrt{3}) = 7 - 6\sqrt{3} \lt 0$ and $f(-\sqrt{3}) = 7 + 6\sqrt{3} \gt 0$

Since the local maximum is positive and the local minimum is negative, the cubic equation has three distinct real roots.

The sum of the roots of the cubic equation $A\lambda^3 + B\lambda^2 + C\lambda + D = 0$ is given by $-\dfrac{B}{A}$.

Here, the coefficient of $\lambda^2$ is $0$.

Sum of all real values of $\lambda = -\dfrac{0}{1} = 0$.

Answer: $0$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: The value of $x$ so that the volume of the parallelopiped formed by the vectors $\hat{i} + x\hat{j} + \hat{k}$, $\hat{j} + x\hat{k}$ and $x\hat{i} + \hat{k}$ is minimum, is
questions.solution:
The volume of the parallelopiped formed by the vectors $\vec{a}$, $\vec{b}$, and $\vec{c}$ is given by the absolute value of their scalar triple product, $V = |[\vec{a}, \vec{b}, \vec{c}]|$.

Given vectors:
$\vec{a} = \hat{i} + x\hat{j} + \hat{k}$
$\vec{b} = 0\hat{i} + \hat{j} + x\hat{k}$
$\vec{c} = x\hat{i} + 0\hat{j} + \hat{k}$

Calculating the scalar triple product:
$[\vec{a}, \vec{b}, \vec{c}] = \begin{vmatrix} 1 & x & 1 \\ 0 & 1 & x \\ x & 0 & 1 \end{vmatrix}$

Expanding the determinant along the first row:
$= 1(1 \times 1 - x \times 0) - x(0 \times 1 - x \times x) + 1(0 \times 0 - 1 \times x)$
$= 1(1) - x(-x^2) + 1(-x)$
$= x^3 - x + 1$

So, the volume is $V = |x^3 - x + 1|$.

Let $f(x) = x^3 - x + 1$. To find the critical points for minimum or maximum volume, we set the first derivative to zero:
$f'(x) = 3x^2 - 1 = 0$
$3x^2 = 1 \Rightarrow x = \pm \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$

Now, checking the second derivative to confirm the minimum:
$f''(x) = 6x$

At $x = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$:
$f''\left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right) = \dfrac{6}{\sqrt{3}} \gt 0$
Since the second derivative is positive, $x = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$ is a point of local minimum.

At $x = -\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$:
$f''\left(-\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right) = -\dfrac{6}{\sqrt{3}} \lt 0$
Since the second derivative is negative, $x = -\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$ is a point of local maximum.

Therefore, the volume of the parallelopiped is minimum when $x = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$.

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $|\vec{a}| = 3$, $|\vec{b}| = 4$, $|\vec{c}| = 5$ such that each vector is perpendicular to the sum of the other two, then $|\vec{a} + \vec{b} + \vec{c}|$ is equal to
questions.solution:
Given that each vector is perpendicular to the sum of the other two, we have:

$\vec{a} \cdot (\vec{b} + \vec{c}) = 0 \Rightarrow \vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} + \vec{a} \cdot \vec{c} = 0$

$\vec{b} \cdot (\vec{c} + \vec{a}) = 0 \Rightarrow \vec{b} \cdot \vec{c} + \vec{b} \cdot \vec{a} = 0$

$\vec{c} \cdot (\vec{a} + \vec{b}) = 0 \Rightarrow \vec{c} \cdot \vec{a} + \vec{c} \cdot \vec{b} = 0$

Adding the above three equations, we get:

$2(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} + \vec{b} \cdot \vec{c} + \vec{c} \cdot \vec{a}) = 0$

Using the identity for the square of the sum of three vectors:

$|\vec{a} + \vec{b} + \vec{c}|^2 = |\vec{a}|^2 + |\vec{b}|^2 + |\vec{c}|^2 + 2(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{b} + \vec{b} \cdot \vec{c} + \vec{c} \cdot \vec{a})$

Substituting the given magnitudes $|\vec{a}| = 3$, $|\vec{b}| = 4$, and $|\vec{c}| = 5$:

$|\vec{a} + \vec{b} + \vec{c}|^2 = 3^2 + 4^2 + 5^2 + 0$

$|\vec{a} + \vec{b} + \vec{c}|^2 = 9 + 16 + 25 = 50$

$|\vec{a} + \vec{b} + \vec{c}| = \sqrt{50} = 5\sqrt{2}$

Answer: $5\sqrt{2}$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.q: If $A(\vec{a})$, $B(\vec{b})$ and $C(\vec{c})$ are vertices of $\triangle ABC$. Point D divides segment BC internally in the ratio $2 : 1$. Point E divides segment AD internally in the ratio $1 : 2$, then the position vector of E is ____
questions.solution:
Point D divides the segment BC internally in the ratio $2 : 1$. Using the section formula, the position vector of D is given by:

$\vec{d} = \dfrac{2\vec{c} + 1\vec{b}}{2 + 1} = \dfrac{\vec{b} + 2\vec{c}}{3}$

Point E divides the segment AD internally in the ratio $1 : 2$. The position vector of E is given by:

$\vec{e} = \dfrac{1\vec{d} + 2\vec{a}}{1 + 2} = \dfrac{2\vec{a} + \vec{d}}{3}$

Substituting the value of $\vec{d}$ into the equation for $\vec{e}$:

$\vec{e} = \dfrac{2\vec{a} + \dfrac{\vec{b} + 2\vec{c}}{3}}{3}$

$\vec{e} = \dfrac{\dfrac{6\vec{a} + \vec{b} + 2\vec{c}}{3}}{3}$

$\vec{e} = \dfrac{6\vec{a} + \vec{b} + 2\vec{c}}{9}$

Answer: $\dfrac{6\vec{a} + \vec{b} + 2\vec{c}}{9}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
In an LCR circuit at resonance, the a.c. source current is
A) maximum in a series LCR circuit only.
B) maximum in a parallel LCR circuit only.
C) maximum in both series and parallel LCR circuits.
D) minimum in both series and parallel LCR circuits.
The correct answer is
questions.solution:
In a series LCR circuit, the impedance is given by $Z = \sqrt{R^2 + (X_L - X_C)^2}$.

At resonance, $X_L = X_C$, which makes the impedance minimum ($Z = R$).

Since $I = \dfrac{V}{Z}$, the current is maximum in a series LCR circuit at resonance.

In a parallel LCR circuit, the admittance is given by $Y = \sqrt{\left(\dfrac{1}{R}\right)^2 + \left(\dfrac{1}{X_C} - \dfrac{1}{X_L}\right)^2}$.

At resonance, $X_L = X_C$, which makes the admittance minimum ($Y = \dfrac{1}{R}$) and the impedance maximum.

Since $I = V Y$, the current is minimum in a parallel LCR circuit at resonance.

Thus, the a.c. source current is maximum in a series LCR circuit only.

Answer: A

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An alternating voltage $e = 150\sqrt{2}\sin 100t$ volt is applied to a capacitor of capacity $2\ \mu\text{F}$. The root mean square value of current in the circuit is
questions.solution:
Given alternating voltage $e = 150\sqrt{2}\sin(100t)$ V.

Comparing with the standard equation $e = E_0\sin(\omega t)$, we get:

Peak voltage $E_0 = 150\sqrt{2}$ V

Angular frequency $\omega = 100$ rad/s

The root mean square voltage is:

$E_{\text{rms}} = \dfrac{E_0}{\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{150\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{2}} = 150$ V

The capacitive reactance is:

$X_C = \dfrac{1}{\omega C} = \dfrac{1}{100 \times 2 \times 10^{-6}} = 5000\ \Omega$

The root mean square current in the circuit is:

$I_{\text{rms}} = \dfrac{E_{\text{rms}}}{X_C} = \dfrac{150}{5000} = 0.03$ A

$I_{\text{rms}} = 30$ mA

Answer: $30$ mA

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: For a series LCR circuit inductive reactance $X_L$ is equal to resistance $R$ and also equal to twice the capacitive reactance $X_C$. The impedance of the circuit and the phase difference between voltage V and current i are respectively
questions.solution:
Given $X_L = R$ and $X_L = 2X_C$.

This gives $X_C = \dfrac{R}{2}$.

The impedance of the series LCR circuit is given by $Z = \sqrt{R^2 + (X_L - X_C)^2}$.

Substituting the values:

$Z = \sqrt{R^2 + \left(R - \dfrac{R}{2}\right)^2} = \sqrt{R^2 + \dfrac{R^2}{4}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{5}R}{2}$.

The phase difference $\phi$ between voltage and current is given by $\tan \phi = \dfrac{X_L - X_C}{R}$.

$\tan \phi = \dfrac{R - \dfrac{R}{2}}{R} = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

$\phi = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)$.

Answer: $\dfrac{\sqrt{5}R}{2},\ \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The shortest wavelength in the Balmer series of hydrogen atom is equal to the shortest wavelength in the Brackett series of a hydrogen like atom of atomic number 'Z'. The value of 'Z' is
questions.solution:
The wavelength of a spectral line is given by Rydberg's formula:

$\dfrac{1}{\lambda} = R Z^2 \left( \dfrac{1}{n_1^2} - \dfrac{1}{n_2^2} \right)$

For the shortest wavelength in the Balmer series of hydrogen ($Z = 1$), $n_1 = 2$ and $n_2 = \infty$:

$\dfrac{1}{\lambda_1} = R (1)^2 \left( \dfrac{1}{2^2} - 0 \right) = \dfrac{R}{4}$

For the shortest wavelength in the Brackett series of a hydrogen-like atom of atomic number $Z$, $n_1 = 4$ and $n_2 = \infty$:

$\dfrac{1}{\lambda_2} = R Z^2 \left( \dfrac{1}{4^2} - 0 \right) = \dfrac{R Z^2}{16}$

Given $\lambda_1 = \lambda_2$, we have:

$\dfrac{R}{4} = \dfrac{R Z^2}{16}$

$Z^2 = 4$

$Z = 2$

Answer: $2$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A slab of material of dielectric constant $K$ has the same area as the plates of a parallel plate capacitor but has a thickness $(4/5)d$, where $d$ is the separation of the plates. The capacitance in the presence and absence of dielectric are $C$ and $C_0$ respectively. The ratio $(C/C_0)$ is
questions.solution:
The capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor without a dielectric is given by:

$C_0 = \dfrac{\varepsilon_0 A}{d}$

When a dielectric slab of thickness $t$ and dielectric constant $K$ is introduced, the capacitance becomes:

$C = \dfrac{\varepsilon_0 A}{d - t + \dfrac{t}{K}}$

Given $t = \dfrac{4}{5}d$, substituting this value yields:

$C = \dfrac{\varepsilon_0 A}{d - \dfrac{4}{5}d + \dfrac{4d}{5K}}$

$C = \dfrac{\varepsilon_0 A}{\dfrac{d}{5} + \dfrac{4d}{5K}}$

$C = \dfrac{\varepsilon_0 A}{\dfrac{d(K + 4)}{5K}}$

$C = \dfrac{5K \varepsilon_0 A}{d(K + 4)}$

Taking the ratio of $C$ to $C_0$ gives:

$\dfrac{C}{C_0} = \dfrac{5K}{K + 4}$

Answer: $\dfrac{5K}{K + 4}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A parallel plate capacitor of capacitance 'C' is connected to a battery and charged to a potential 'V'. Another capacitor of capacitance '$3C$' is charged to a potential '$3V$'. The charging battery is then disconnected and both the capacitors are connected in parallel to each other such that positive terminal of one is connected to negative terminal of the other. The final energy of the configuration is
questions.solution:
Initial charge on the first capacitor, $Q_1 = CV$

Initial charge on the second capacitor, $Q_2 = (3C)(3V) = 9CV$

When connected in parallel with opposite polarities, the net charge is $Q = Q_2 - Q_1 = 9CV - CV = 8CV$

Equivalent capacitance of the parallel combination is $C_{eq} = C + 3C = 4C$

Final energy of the configuration is given by $U = \dfrac{Q^2}{2C_{eq}}$

Substituting the values, $U = \dfrac{(8CV)^2}{2(4C)} = \dfrac{64C^2V^2}{8C} = 8CV^2$

Answer: $8.0\,CV^2$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The voltage across a lamp is $(6.0 \pm 0.3)$ volt and the current passing through it is $(4.0 \pm 0.1)$ ampere. The power consumed in watt will be (using percentage error)
questions.solution:
Power is given by $P = VI$

Substituting the given values:

$P = 6.0 \times 4.0 = 24.0$ W

The relative error in power is given by:

$\dfrac{\Delta P}{P} = \dfrac{\Delta V}{V} + \dfrac{\Delta I}{I}$

$\dfrac{\Delta P}{24.0} = \dfrac{0.3}{6.0} + \dfrac{0.1}{4.0}$

$\dfrac{\Delta P}{24.0} = 0.05 + 0.025 = 0.075$

$\Delta P = 24.0 \times 0.075 = 1.8$ W

The power consumed is $(24.0 \pm 1.8)$ W.

Answer: $(24.0 \pm 1.8)$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In a potentiometer circuit when two cells of e.m.f. $1.5$ volt and $1.2$ volt are connected to assist each other, balancing length is $270$ cm. What will be the balancing length in cm when these two cells are connected in opposition?
questions.solution:
Let the potential gradient of the potentiometer wire be $k$.

When the cells assist each other, the equivalent EMF is $E_1 + E_2$.

$E_1 + E_2 = k l_1$

$1.5 + 1.2 = k \times 270$

$2.7 = 270 k$

When the cells are connected in opposition, the equivalent EMF is $E_1 - E_2$.

$E_1 - E_2 = k l_2$

$1.5 - 1.2 = k l_2$

$0.3 = k l_2$

Dividing the two equations, we get:

$\dfrac{2.7}{0.3} = \dfrac{270}{l_2}$

$9 = \dfrac{270}{l_2}$

$l_2 = 30$ cm

Answer: $30$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In a meter bridge experiment, the balance point is obtained at length '$l_1$' cm from left hand when resistances in the left gap and right gap are $15 \ \Omega$ and $R \ \Omega$ respectively. When the resistance $R$ is shunted with equal resistance the new balance point is at $(1.6\,l_1)$. The resistance $R$ in ohm is
questions.solution:
For a meter bridge, the balance condition is given by $\dfrac{R_1}{R_2} = \dfrac{l}{100 - l}$.

Initially, the resistances are $15 \ \Omega$ and $R \ \Omega$, and the balance point is at $l_1$.

$\dfrac{15}{R} = \dfrac{l_1}{100 - l_1}$

When $R$ is shunted with an equal resistance $R$, the equivalent resistance in the right gap becomes $\dfrac{R \times R}{R + R} = \dfrac{R}{2}$. The new balance point is at $1.6 l_1$.

$\dfrac{15}{\dfrac{R}{2}} = \dfrac{1.6 l_1}{100 - 1.6 l_1}$

$\dfrac{30}{R} = \dfrac{1.6 l_1}{100 - 1.6 l_1}$

Dividing the second equation by the first equation:

$\dfrac{\dfrac{30}{R}}{\dfrac{15}{R}} = \dfrac{\dfrac{1.6 l_1}{100 - 1.6 l_1}}{\dfrac{l_1}{100 - l_1}}$

$2 = \dfrac{1.6(100 - l_1)}{100 - 1.6 l_1}$

$200 - 3.2 l_1 = 160 - 1.6 l_1$

$1.6 l_1 = 40 \Rightarrow l_1 = 25$

Substituting $l_1 = 25$ into the first equation:

$\dfrac{15}{R} = \dfrac{25}{100 - 25}$

$\dfrac{15}{R} = \dfrac{25}{75} = \dfrac{1}{3}$

$R = 15 \times 3 = 45 \ \Omega$

Answer: $45$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: According to Einstein's photoelectric equation, the graph of the kinetic energy of the emitted photoelectrons versus the frequency of incident radiation gives a straight line whose slope
options: depends on the intensity of incident radiation.
depends on the nature of the metal used.
is the same for all metals and independent of the intensity of radiation.
depends on both the intensity of incident radiation and the nature of metal used.
questions.solution:
ation, and $\Phi$ is the work function of the metal.

Comparing this with the equation of a straight line $y = mx + c$, we get the slope $m = h$.

Since Planck's constant $h$ is a universal constant, the slope of the graph is the same for all metals and is completely independent of the intensity of the incident radiation.

Answer: is the same for all metals and independent of the intensity of radiation.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A photoelectric surface is illuminated successively by monochromatic light of wavelength $\lambda$ and $(\lambda/3)$. If the maximum kinetic energy of the emitted photo electrons in the second case is $4$ times that in the first case, the work function of the surface of the material is ($h$ = Planck's constant, $c$ = speed of light)
questions.solution:
Using Einstein's photoelectric equation, the maximum kinetic energy of emitted photoelectrons is given by $K = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda} - \phi$, where $\phi$ is the work function of the material.

For the first case with wavelength $\lambda$:
$K_1 = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda} - \phi$

For the second case with wavelength $\dfrac{\lambda}{3}$:
$K_2 = \dfrac{hc}{\dfrac{\lambda}{3}} - \phi = \dfrac{3hc}{\lambda} - \phi$

It is given that the maximum kinetic energy in the second case is $4$ times that in the first case:
$K_2 = 4K_1$

Substituting the expressions for $K_1$ and $K_2$:
$\dfrac{3hc}{\lambda} - \phi = 4\left(\dfrac{hc}{\lambda} - \phi\right)$

$\dfrac{3hc}{\lambda} - \phi = \dfrac{4hc}{\lambda} - 4\phi$

$4\phi - \phi = \dfrac{4hc}{\lambda} - \dfrac{3hc}{\lambda}$

$3\phi = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda}$

$\phi = \dfrac{hc}{3\lambda}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Magnetic flux linked with the coil in weber is given by the equation $\Phi = 5t^2 + 6t + 11$. The e.m.f. induced in the coil in the $5^{\text{th}}$ second will be
questions.solution:
The magnetic flux is given by $\Phi = 5t^2 + 6t + 11$.

The e.m.f. induced in the $5^{\text{th}}$ second is the average e.m.f. from $t = 4$ s to $t = 5$ s.

The magnitude of the average induced e.m.f. is $e = \dfrac{\Delta \Phi}{\Delta t} = \dfrac{\Phi(5) - \Phi(4)}{5 - 4}$.

$\Phi(5) = 5(5)^2 + 6(5) + 11 = 125 + 30 + 11 = 166$ Wb

$\Phi(4) = 5(4)^2 + 6(4) + 11 = 80 + 24 + 11 = 115$ Wb

$e = \dfrac{166 - 115}{1} = 51$ V

Answer: $51$ V

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Consider two coils in which a current in one coil carrying $6$ A causes the change in the flux in the second coil $12 \times 10^{-4}$ weber/turn. The second coil has $2000$ turns. The mutual inductance between the coils is
questions.solution:
The total flux linkage in the second coil is given by $\Phi_2 = N_2 \phi_2$.

Given $N_2 = 2000$ and $\phi_2 = 12 \times 10^{-4}$ Wb/turn.

$\Phi_2 = 2000 \times 12 \times 10^{-4} = 2.4$ Wb.

The mutual inductance $M$ is defined by the relation $\Phi_2 = M I_1$.

Given $I_1 = 6$ A.

$M = \dfrac{\Phi_2}{I_1} = \dfrac{2.4}{6} = 0.4$ H.

Answer: $0.4$ H

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two different coils have self-inductance $3L$ and $L$. The current in both the coils is increased at the same constant rate. At certain instant of time, the power given to the two coils is same. At that time there was current and voltage induced in the two coils. At the same instant, the ratio of energy stored in the first coil to that in the second coil is
questions.solution:
Let the self-inductances of the two coils be $L_1 = 3L$ and $L_2 = L$.

The rate of change of current is the same for both coils, so $\dfrac{di_1}{dt} = \dfrac{di_2}{dt}$.

The induced voltage in a coil is given by $V = L \dfrac{di}{dt}$.

For the two coils, the induced voltages are:
$V_1 = 3L \dfrac{di_1}{dt}$
$V_2 = L \dfrac{di_2}{dt}$

The power given to the coils is $P = Vi$. Since the power is the same at the given instant:
$P_1 = P_2$

$V_1 i_1 = V_2 i_2$

$3L \dfrac{di_1}{dt} i_1 = L \dfrac{di_2}{dt} i_2$

$3 i_1 = i_2$

The energy stored in an inductor is $U = \dfrac{1}{2} L i^2$.

The ratio of the energy stored in the first coil to that in the second coil is:
$\dfrac{U_1}{U_2} = \dfrac{\dfrac{1}{2} L_1 i_1^2}{\dfrac{1}{2} L_2 i_2^2}$

$\dfrac{U_1}{U_2} = \dfrac{3L}{L} \left( \dfrac{i_1}{i_2} \right)^2$

$\dfrac{U_1}{U_2} = 3 \left( \dfrac{1}{3} \right)^2 = \dfrac{3}{9} = \dfrac{1}{3}$

Answer: $1:3$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two electric dipoles of moment $P$ and $8P$ are placed in opposite directions on a line at a distance of $24$ cm. The electric field will be zero at the point between the dipoles whose distance from the dipole of moment $P$ will be $x_1$. When $8P$ is replaced by $27P$ keeping all other quantities the same, the distance $x_1$ now becomes $x_2$. The difference $|x_2 - x_1|$ is ( All the distances are measured from the centers of the dipole.)
questions.solution:
Let the distance of the null point from the dipole of moment $P$ be $x$. The distance from the second dipole is $24 - x$.

The electric field due to a short dipole on its axis at a distance $r$ is given by $E = \dfrac{2kP}{r^3}$.

For the net electric field to be zero, the magnitudes of the electric fields due to both dipoles must be equal.

Case 1: Dipoles are $P$ and $8P$
$\dfrac{2kP}{x_1^3} = \dfrac{2k(8P)}{(24 - x_1)^3}$

Taking the cube root on both sides:
$\dfrac{1}{x_1} = \dfrac{2}{24 - x_1}$

$24 - x_1 = 2x_1 \Rightarrow 3x_1 = 24 \Rightarrow x_1 = 8$ cm

Case 2: Dipole $8P$ is replaced by $27P$
$\dfrac{2kP}{x_2^3} = \dfrac{2k(27P)}{(24 - x_2)^3}$

Taking the cube root on both sides:
$\dfrac{1}{x_2} = \dfrac{3}{24 - x_2}$

$24 - x_2 = 3x_2 \Rightarrow 4x_2 = 24 \Rightarrow x_2 = 6$ cm

The difference is $|x_2 - x_1| = |6 - 8| = 2$ cm.

Answer: $2$ cm

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: '$n$' small spherical drops of the same size which are charged to 'V' volt each coalesce to form a single big drop. The potential of a big drop is
questions.solution:
Let the radius of each small drop be $r$ and its charge be $q$.

The potential of each small drop is $V = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0}\dfrac{q}{r}$.

When $n$ such drops coalesce, the total charge of the big drop is $Q = nq$.

The volume is conserved, so the volume of the big drop is equal to the sum of the volumes of the $n$ small drops.

$\dfrac{4}{3}\pi R^3 = n \left(\dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3\right)$

$R^3 = n r^3$

$R = n^{\frac{1}{3}} r$

The potential of the single big drop is:

$V' = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0}\dfrac{Q}{R}$

$V' = \dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0}\dfrac{nq}{n^{\frac{1}{3}} r}$

$V' = n^{1 - \frac{1}{3}} \left(\dfrac{1}{4\pi\epsilon_0}\dfrac{q}{r}\right)$

$V' = n^{\frac{2}{3}} V$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A geostationary satellite is orbiting the earth at a height of $4R$ above the surface of the earth, where $R$ is the radius of the earth. Another satellite is orbiting the earth at a height $1.5R$ from the surface of the earth with periodic time 'T' in hour. The value of 'T' in hour is
questions.solution:
The orbital radius of the geostationary satellite is $r_1 = R + 4R = 5R$.

The time period of a geostationary satellite is $T_1 = 24$ hours.

The orbital radius of the second satellite is $r_2 = R + 1.5R = 2.5R$.

Let the time period of the second satellite be $T_2 = T$.

According to Kepler's third law, the square of the time period is proportional to the cube of the orbital radius:

$T^2 \propto r^3$

$\left(\dfrac{T_2}{T_1}\right)^2 = \left(\dfrac{r_2}{r_1}\right)^3$

$\left(\dfrac{T}{24}\right)^2 = \left(\dfrac{2.5R}{5R}\right)^3$

$\left(\dfrac{T}{24}\right)^2 = \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^3 = \dfrac{1}{8}$

$\dfrac{T}{24} = \dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}$

$T = \dfrac{24}{2\sqrt{2}} = 6\sqrt{2}$ hours

Answer: $6\sqrt{2}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The kinetic energy of an ideal gas is $E_0$ at $27^\circ\text{C}$. When the temperature is increased to $177^\circ\text{C}$, then kinetic energy will be
questions.solution:
The kinetic energy of an ideal gas is directly proportional to its absolute temperature.

$E \propto T$

Initial temperature $T_1 = 27^\circ\text{C} = 27 + 273 = 300\text{ K}$

Final temperature $T_2 = 177^\circ\text{C} = 177 + 273 = 450\text{ K}$

Using the relation $\dfrac{E_1}{T_1} = \dfrac{E_2}{T_2}$:

$\dfrac{E_0}{300} = \dfrac{E_2}{450}$

$E_2 = E_0 \times \dfrac{450}{300} = \dfrac{3E_0}{2}$

Answer: $3E_0 / 2$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Which of the following person is in an inertial frame of reference?
options: A pilot in an aeroplane which is taking off.
A driver driving a bus which is moving with constant velocity.
A child revolving in a merry - go - round.
A man in a train which is slowing down to stop.
questions.solution:
An inertial frame of reference is a frame that is non-accelerating. It is either at rest or moving with a constant velocity.

An aeroplane taking off has a net forward acceleration, making it a non-inertial frame.

A child revolving in a merry-go-round undergoes circular motion and experiences centripetal acceleration, making it a non-inertial frame.

A train slowing down is decelerating, meaning it has a non-zero acceleration, making it a non-inertial frame.

A bus moving with constant velocity has zero acceleration. Therefore, the driver in the bus is in an inertial frame of reference.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two thin long parallel wires, $W_1$ and $W_2$ separated by distance '$a$', carry currents $i$ and $3i$ respectively in the same direction. The magnitude of the force per unit length exerted by wire $W_1$ on wire $W_2$ is
questions.solution:
The magnetic field produced by wire $W_1$ at the position of wire $W_2$ is

$B_1 = \dfrac{\mu_0 i}{2\pi a}$

The magnetic force experienced by wire $W_2$ per unit length is

$\dfrac{F}{L} = B_1 I_2$

Substituting $I_2 = 3i$, we get

$\dfrac{F}{L} = \left(\dfrac{\mu_0 i}{2\pi a}\right) (3i) = \dfrac{3\mu_0 i^2}{2\pi a}$

Answer: $\dfrac{3\mu_0\, i^2}{2\pi\, a}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two circular coils X (smaller) and Y (bigger), each having a single turn, carry equal currents in the same direction and subtend the same angle at point 'O' along the axis of the coil. The distances of the centers of coil to point 'O' are $d$ and $\left(\dfrac{d}{2}\right)$ for coil Y and X respectively. The radii of coils Y and X are $(2r)$ and $(r)$ respectively. The magnetic induction due to the bigger coil at point 'O' is $B_y$ and that due to smaller coil X at point 'O' is $B_x$. ($d \gg r$) The relation between $B_x$ and $B_y$ is
questions.solution:
The magnetic field on the axis of a circular coil of radius $R$ at a distance $x$ from its center is given by:

$B = \dfrac{\mu_0 I R^2}{2(R^2 + x^2)^{3/2}}$

For coil Y (bigger coil):
Radius $R_y = 2r$, distance $x_y = d$.

$B_y = \dfrac{\mu_0 I (2r)^2}{2((2r)^2 + d^2)^{3/2}} = \dfrac{4\mu_0 I r^2}{2(4r^2 + d^2)^{3/2}} = \dfrac{2\mu_0 I r^2}{(4r^2 + d^2)^{3/2}}$

For coil X (smaller coil):
Radius $R_x = r$, distance $x_x = \dfrac{d}{2}$.

$B_x = \dfrac{\mu_0 I r^2}{2\left(r^2 + \left(\dfrac{d}{2}\right)^2\right)^{3/2}} = \dfrac{\mu_0 I r^2}{2\left(\dfrac{4r^2 + d^2}{4}\right)^{3/2}} = \dfrac{8\mu_0 I r^2}{2(4r^2 + d^2)^{3/2}} = \dfrac{4\mu_0 I r^2}{(4r^2 + d^2)^{3/2}}$

Comparing the expressions for $B_x$ and $B_y$, we get:

$B_x = 2B_y$

Answer: $B_x = 2B_y$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The frequency of oscillation of a small magnet in a magnetic field of induction 'B' is '$n$'. If the frequency of oscillations of the same magnet in a field of induction 'X' falls to $\left(\dfrac{n}{3}\right)$, the value of 'X' is
questions.solution:
The frequency of oscillation of a magnet in a magnetic field is given by

$n = \dfrac{1}{2\pi} \sqrt{\dfrac{MB}{I}}$

Since the same magnet is used, $M$ and $I$ are constant. Thus, $n \propto \sqrt{B}$, which implies $B \propto n^2$.

Given $n_1 = n$ at $B_1 = B$, and $n_2 = \dfrac{n}{3}$ at $B_2 = X$.

$\dfrac{B_1}{B_2} = \left(\dfrac{n_1}{n_2}\right)^2$

$\dfrac{B}{X} = \left(\dfrac{n}{n/3}\right)^2 = 3^2 = 9$

$X = \dfrac{B}{9}$

Answer: $\dfrac{B}{9}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A diamagnetic liquid is filled in a U-tube. One arm of a U-tube is placed in an external magnetic field with the meniscus in line with the field. The level of the liquid in that arm will
questions.solution:
Diamagnetic substances are repelled by magnetic fields and tend to move from regions of stronger magnetic field to regions of weaker magnetic field.

When one arm of the U-tube containing a diamagnetic liquid is placed in an external magnetic field, the liquid experiences a force pushing it away from the stronger field region.

As a result, the level of the liquid in the arm placed in the magnetic field will fall.

Answer: fall.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
For two vectors $\vec{P}$ and $\vec{Q}$, $\vec{P} \cdot \vec{Q} = |\vec{P} \times \vec{Q}|$
The magnitude of $\vec{R} = \vec{P} + \vec{Q}$ is ($\cos 45^\circ = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$) ?
questions.solution:
Given $\vec{P} \cdot \vec{Q} = |\vec{P} \times \vec{Q}|$

$PQ \cos \theta = PQ \sin \theta$

$\tan \theta = 1 \Rightarrow \theta = 45^\circ$

The magnitude of the resultant vector $\vec{R} = \vec{P} + \vec{Q}$ is given by:

$|\vec{R}| = \sqrt{P^2 + Q^2 + 2PQ \cos \theta}$

Substituting $\theta = 45^\circ$:

$|\vec{R}| = \sqrt{P^2 + Q^2 + 2PQ \cos 45^\circ}$

$|\vec{R}| = \sqrt{P^2 + Q^2 + 2PQ \left(\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)}$

$|\vec{R}| = \sqrt{P^2 + Q^2 + \sqrt{2}PQ}$

Answer: $\sqrt{P^2 + Q^2 + \sqrt{2}\,PQ}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: An in-compressible fluid flows steadily through a horizontal cylindrical pipe. The pipe has radius '$3R$' at point A and '$1.5R$' at point B, further along the flow direction at the same level. If the velocity at point A is '$v$', then that at point B is
questions.solution:
Using the equation of continuity for an incompressible fluid:

$A_A v_A = A_B v_B$

$\pi (3R)^2 v = \pi (1.5R)^2 v_B$

$9 \pi R^2 v = 2.25 \pi R^2 v_B$

$v_B = \dfrac{9}{2.25} v = 4v$

Answer: $4v$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The pressures inside two soap bubbles A and B are $1.02$ atmosphere and $1.04$ atmosphere respectively. The ratio of volume of bubble A to that of bubble B is (outside pressure $= 1$ atmosphere)
questions.solution:
The excess pressure inside a soap bubble is given by $\Delta P = \dfrac{4T}{R}$, where $T$ is the surface tension and $R$ is the radius of the bubble.

For bubble A, the excess pressure is $\Delta P_A = 1.02 - 1 = 0.02$ atm.

For bubble B, the excess pressure is $\Delta P_B = 1.04 - 1 = 0.04$ atm.

Taking the ratio of the excess pressures, we get $\dfrac{\Delta P_A}{\Delta P_B} = \dfrac{0.02}{0.04} = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

Since $R \propto \dfrac{1}{\Delta P}$, the ratio of their radii is $\dfrac{R_A}{R_B} = \dfrac{\Delta P_B}{\Delta P_A} = \dfrac{2}{1}$.

The volume of a spherical bubble is $V = \dfrac{4}{3}\pi R^3$, which means $V \propto R^3$.

The ratio of their volumes is $\dfrac{V_A}{V_B} = \left(\dfrac{R_A}{R_B}\right)^3 = (2)^3 = 8$.

Thus, the ratio of the volume of bubble A to that of bubble B is $8:1$.

Answer: $8:1$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: One large soap bubble of diameter 'D' breaks into $64$ bubbles having surface tension 'T'. The change in surface energy is
questions.solution:
Let $R$ be the radius of the large bubble and $r$ be the radius of each small bubble.

Equating the initial and final volumes:

$\dfrac{4}{3}\pi R^3 = 64 \times \dfrac{4}{3}\pi r^3$

$R^3 = 64 r^3 \Rightarrow r = \dfrac{R}{4}$

A soap bubble has two free surfaces. The initial surface energy is:

$U_i = T \times 2 \times 4\pi R^2 = 8\pi R^2 T$

The final surface energy of $64$ small bubbles is:

$U_f = 64 \times T \times 2 \times 4\pi r^2 = 512\pi r^2 T$

Substituting $r = \dfrac{R}{4}$:

$U_f = 512\pi \left(\dfrac{R}{4}\right)^2 T = 512\pi \dfrac{R^2}{16} T = 32\pi R^2 T$

The change in surface energy is:

$\Delta U = U_f - U_i = 32\pi R^2 T - 8\pi R^2 T = 24\pi R^2 T$

Given the diameter $D = 2R$, we substitute $R = \dfrac{D}{2}$:

$\Delta U = 24\pi \left(\dfrac{D}{2}\right)^2 T = 24\pi \dfrac{D^2}{4} T = 6\pi TD^2$

Answer: $6\pi TD^2$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two particles having mass 'M' and 'm' are moving in a circular path with radius 'R' and 'r' respectively. The time period for both the particles is same. The ratio of angular velocity of the first particle to that of the second particle will be
questions.solution:
Angular velocity is given by $\omega = \dfrac{2\pi}{T}$

Since the time period $T$ is the same for both particles, their angular velocities are equal.

$\omega_1 = \dfrac{2\pi}{T}$ and $\omega_2 = \dfrac{2\pi}{T}$

$\dfrac{\omega_1}{\omega_2} = \dfrac{1}{1}$

The ratio of their angular velocities is $1:1$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two stones of masses $m$ and $3m$ are whirled in horizontal circles, the heavier one in a radius $\dfrac{r}{3}$ and the lighter one in radius $r$. When both the stones experience same centripetal forces, the tangential speed of lighter stone is '$n$' times that of the value of heavier stone. The value of '$n$' is
questions.solution:
Let the mass, radius, and tangential speed of the lighter stone be $m_1 = m$, $r_1 = r$, and $v_1$ respectively.

Let the mass, radius, and tangential speed of the heavier stone be $m_2 = 3m$, $r_2 = \dfrac{r}{3}$, and $v_2$ respectively.

The centripetal force on the lighter stone is $F_1 = \dfrac{m_1 v_1^2}{r_1} = \dfrac{m v_1^2}{r}$.

The centripetal force on the heavier stone is $F_2 = \dfrac{m_2 v_2^2}{r_2} = \dfrac{3m v_2^2}{\dfrac{r}{3}} = \dfrac{9m v_2^2}{r}$.

Given that both stones experience the same centripetal force, $F_1 = F_2$.

$\dfrac{m v_1^2}{r} = \dfrac{9m v_2^2}{r}$

$v_1^2 = 9 v_2^2$

$v_1 = 3 v_2$

Since the tangential speed of the lighter stone is $n$ times that of the heavier stone, $n = 3$.

Answer: $3$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A radioactive sample has half-life of $5$ years. The percentage of fraction decayed in $10$ years will be
questions.solution:
Given half-life $T_{1/2} = 5$ years and time $t = 10$ years.

Number of half-lives $n = \dfrac{t}{T_{1/2}} = \dfrac{10}{5} = 2$

Fraction of sample remaining after $n$ half-lives is given by $\dfrac{N}{N_0} = \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^n$

$\dfrac{N}{N_0} = \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^2 = \dfrac{1}{4}$

Fraction of sample decayed $= 1 - \dfrac{N}{N_0} = 1 - \dfrac{1}{4} = \dfrac{3}{4}$

Percentage of fraction decayed $= \dfrac{3}{4} \times 100\% = 75\%$

Answer: $75\%$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
A particle executes a simple harmonic motion with a periodic time $8$ second. At time $t = 0$, it is at a mean position. The ratio of the distance traveled by a particle in the 2nd and that in the 1st second of its motion is
($\sin 45^\circ = \cos 45^\circ = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$, $\sin 90^\circ = \cos 0^\circ = 1$)
questions.solution:
The time period of the simple harmonic motion is $T = 8$ s.

The angular frequency is $\omega = \dfrac{2\pi}{T} = \dfrac{2\pi}{8} = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$ rad/s.

Since the particle starts from the mean position at $t = 0$, its displacement equation is given by:
$x(t) = A \sin(\omega t) = A \sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4} t\right)$

The distance traveled by the particle in the 1st second ($t = 0$ to $t = 1$ s) is:
$D_1 = x(1) - x(0) = A \sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) - 0 = \dfrac{A}{\sqrt{2}}$

The distance traveled by the particle in the 2nd second ($t = 1$ to $t = 2$ s) is:
$D_2 = x(2) - x(1) = A \sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) - A \sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = A - \dfrac{A}{\sqrt{2}}$

The ratio of the distance traveled in the 2nd second to that in the 1st second is:
$\dfrac{D_2}{D_1} = \dfrac{A - \dfrac{A}{\sqrt{2}}}{\dfrac{A}{\sqrt{2}}} = \dfrac{1 - \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}}{\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}} = \sqrt{2} - 1$

Answer: $\sqrt{2} - 1$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A glass slab of thickness $6.0$ cm is placed on the piece of paper on which an inkdot is marked. By how much distance would an inkdot appear to be raised? The velocity of light in glass is $2 \times 10^8 \text{ ms}^{-1}$ and that in air is $3 \times 10^8 \text{ ms}^{-1}$.
questions.solution:
The refractive index of glass is given by $\mu = \dfrac{c}{v_g}$

$\mu = \dfrac{3 \times 10^8}{2 \times 10^8} = 1.5 = \dfrac{3}{2}$

The apparent shift of the inkdot is given by the formula $\Delta x = t \left(1 - \dfrac{1}{\mu}\right)$

Substituting the given values:

$\Delta x = 6.0 \left(1 - \dfrac{2}{3}\right)$

$\Delta x = 6.0 \times \dfrac{1}{3} = 2.0 \text{ cm}$

The inkdot appears to be raised by $2.0 \text{ cm}$.

Answer: $2.0$ cm

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The radius of gyration of a solid sphere of radius 'R' and mass 'M' about its diameter is $K_d$ and that about a tangent of a solid sphere is $K_t$. The ratio of $K_d$ to $K_t$ is
questions.solution:
The moment of inertia of a solid sphere about its diameter is $I_d = \dfrac{2}{5}MR^2$.

The radius of gyration about the diameter is $K_d = \sqrt{\dfrac{2}{5}}R$.

Using the parallel axis theorem, the moment of inertia of the solid sphere about a tangent is $I_t = I_d + MR^2 = \dfrac{2}{5}MR^2 + MR^2 = \dfrac{7}{5}MR^2$.

The radius of gyration about the tangent is $K_t = \sqrt{\dfrac{7}{5}}R$.

The ratio of $K_d$ to $K_t$ is $\dfrac{K_d}{K_t} = \dfrac{\sqrt{\dfrac{2}{5}}R}{\sqrt{\dfrac{7}{5}}R} = \left(\dfrac{2}{7}\right)^{1/2}$.

Answer: $\left(\dfrac{2}{7}\right)^{1/2}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
A thin uniform rod AB of mass '$m$' and length '$l$' is hinged at one end A to the ground level. Initially the rod stands vertically and is allowed to fall freely to the ground in the vertical plane. The angular velocity of the rod when its B end strikes the ground is
($g$ = acceleration due to gravity)
questions.solution:
By the principle of conservation of mechanical energy, the loss in potential energy of the rod is equal to the gain in its rotational kinetic energy.

The initial height of the center of mass of the rod is $h_i = \dfrac{l}{2}$ and the final height is $h_f = 0$.

Loss in potential energy $= mg\left(\dfrac{l}{2}\right)$

Gain in rotational kinetic energy $= \dfrac{1}{2}I\omega^2$

The moment of inertia of the rod about the hinged end A is $I = \dfrac{ml^2}{3}$.

Equating the two energies:

$mg\left(\dfrac{l}{2}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{ml^2}{3}\right)\omega^2$

$mgl = \dfrac{ml^2}{3}\omega^2$

$\omega^2 = \dfrac{3g}{l}$

$\omega = \sqrt{\dfrac{3g}{l}}$

Answer: $\sqrt{\dfrac{3g}{l}}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
In n-type semiconductor
A) pentavalent impurity are dopants and holes are majority carriers.
B) trivalent impurity are dopants and electrons are minority carriers.
C) pentavalent impurity are dopants and electrons are majority carriers.
D) trivalent impurity are dopants and holes are majority carriers.
questions.solution:
An n-type semiconductor is obtained by doping an intrinsic semiconductor with pentavalent impurity atoms such as Phosphorus, Arsenic, or Antimony.

Each pentavalent atom donates one extra electron to the crystal lattice, making electrons the majority charge carriers.

Holes are generated only by thermal excitation and act as the minority charge carriers.

Therefore, in an n-type semiconductor, pentavalent impurities are the dopants and electrons are the majority carriers.

Answer: C

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: For a two input logic gate, when the inputs are 'zero' and 'zero' the output is 'one'. When the inputs are 'one' and 'zero' the output is 'zero'. The type of logic gate is
questions.solution:
Let the inputs be $A$ and $B$, and the output be $Y$.

Given conditions:
When $A = 0$ and $B = 0$, $Y = 1$.
When $A = 1$ and $B = 0$, $Y = 0$.

Checking the given options:
For a NAND gate: $Y = \overline{A \cdot B}$. If $A = 1, B = 0$, $Y = \overline{0} = 1$. This does not match.
For an OR gate: $Y = A + B$. If $A = 0, B = 0$, $Y = 0$. This does not match.
For a NOR gate: $Y = \overline{A + B}$. If $A = 0, B = 0$, $Y = \overline{0} = 1$. If $A = 1, B = 0$, $Y = \overline{1} = 0$. This matches both conditions.
For an XOR gate: $Y = A \oplus B$. If $A = 0, B = 0$, $Y = 0$. This does not match.

Therefore, the logic gate is a NOR gate.

Answer: NOR

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
The material used for solar cell should have band gap
(A) equal to zero.
(B) equal to $0.08$ eV.
(C) between $1.0$ eV to $1.8$ eV.
(D) equal to $2$ eV.
questions.solution:
The solar spectrum has maximum intensity at an energy of about $1.5$ eV.

To maximize the absorption of solar radiation and the efficiency of the solar cell, the band gap of the semiconductor should be close to $1.5$ eV.

Commonly used materials for solar cells include Silicon ($E_g \approx 1.1$ eV) and GaAs ($E_g \approx 1.43$ eV).

Therefore, the ideal band gap for a solar cell material is between $1.0$ eV and $1.8$ eV.

Answer: C

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If the two temperatures on Fahrenheit scale differ by $54^\circ\text{F}$, then the difference in temperature on the Celsius scale is
questions.solution:
The relation between the Fahrenheit and Celsius temperature scales is given by:

$F = \dfrac{9}{5}C + 32$

Taking the difference for two temperatures, we get:

$\Delta F = \dfrac{9}{5}\Delta C$

Given that the difference on the Fahrenheit scale is $\Delta F = 54^{\circ}\text{F}$, substituting this value yields:

$54 = \dfrac{9}{5}\Delta C$

$\Delta C = 54 \times \dfrac{5}{9}$

$\Delta C = 30^{\circ}\text{C}$

The difference in temperature on the Celsius scale is $30^{\circ}\text{C}$.

Answer: $30^\circ\text{C}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A black body is at temperature $827^\circ\text{C}$. The rate at which it emits energy is proportional to
questions.solution:
According to the Stefan-Boltzmann law, the rate at which a black body emits energy is directly proportional to the fourth power of its absolute temperature.

$E \propto T^4$

The given temperature is $t = 827^\circ\text{C}$.

Converting this to absolute temperature in Kelvin:

$T = 827 + 273 = 1100 \text{ K}$

Therefore, the rate of energy emission is proportional to $(1100)^4$.

Answer: $(1100)^4$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: When $170$ J of energy is incident on a surface of a body, $17$ J of energy is reflected by it. If the coefficient of absorption is $0.7$, then the amount of energy transmitted will be
questions.solution:
Coefficient of reflection, $r = \dfrac{Q_r}{Q} = \dfrac{17}{170} = 0.1$

Coefficient of transmission, $t = 1 - (a + r) = 1 - (0.7 + 0.1) = 0.2$

Transmitted energy, $Q_t = t Q = 0.2 \times 170 = 34$ J

Answer: $34.0$ J

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The thermodynamic process in which no work is done by the gas or on the gas is
questions.solution:
Work done by a gas in a thermodynamic process is given by $W = \int P dV$.

For no work to be done by the gas or on the gas, $W = 0$, which implies $dV = 0$.

This means the change in volume is zero, so the volume remains constant throughout the process.

A thermodynamic process in which the volume remains constant is called an isochoric process.

Answer: isochoric process

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A gas at normal temperature is suddenly compressed to one-fourth of its original volume. If $\gamma = 1.5$, then the increase in the temperature of the gas in Kelvin is ($\gamma$ is the ratio of specific heats)
questions.solution:
Normal temperature is $T_1 = 273$ K.

Initial volume $V_1 = V$.

Final volume $V_2 = \dfrac{V}{4}$.

Since the gas is suddenly compressed, the process is adiabatic.

The relation between temperature and volume for an adiabatic process is $T V^{\gamma - 1} = \text{constant}$.

$T_1 V_1^{\gamma - 1} = T_2 V_2^{\gamma - 1}$

$T_2 = T_1 \left( \dfrac{V_1}{V_2} \right)^{\gamma - 1}$

Substituting the given values:

$T_2 = 273 \left( \dfrac{V}{V/4} \right)^{1.5 - 1}$

$T_2 = 273 (4)^{0.5}$

$T_2 = 273 \times 2 = 546$ K.

The increase in temperature is $\Delta T = T_2 - T_1$.

$\Delta T = 546 - 273 = 273$ K.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In Young's double slit experiment, for the $n^{\text{th}}$ dark fringe ($n = 1, 2, 3, \ldots$) the phase difference of the interfering waves in radian will be
questions.solution:
For destructive interference (dark fringes) in Young's double slit experiment, the path difference $\Delta x$ is an odd multiple of $\dfrac{\lambda}{2}$.

For the $n^{\text{th}}$ dark fringe, where $n = 1, 2, 3, \ldots$, the path difference is given by:

$\Delta x = (2n - 1)\dfrac{\lambda}{2}$

The phase difference $\Delta \phi$ is related to the path difference by:

$\Delta \phi = \dfrac{2\pi}{\lambda} \Delta x$

Substituting the value of $\Delta x$:

$\Delta \phi = \dfrac{2\pi}{\lambda} \times (2n - 1)\dfrac{\lambda}{2}$

$\Delta \phi = (2n - 1)\pi$

Answer: $(2n - 1)\pi$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In a single slit diffraction pattern, the distance between the plane of the slit and the screen is $1.4$ m. The width of the slit is $0.66$ mm. The second maximum is formed at the distance of $2.8$ mm from the center of the screen. The wavelength of light used is
questions.solution:
The position of the $n$-th secondary maximum in a single slit diffraction pattern is given by:

$y_n = \dfrac{(2n + 1)\lambda D}{2a}$

For the second maximum, $n = 2$:

$y_2 = \dfrac{5\lambda D}{2a}$

Rearranging for the wavelength $\lambda$:

$\lambda = \dfrac{2a y_2}{5D}$

Given values are:
$D = 1.4$ m
$a = 0.66$ mm $= 0.66 \times 10^{-3}$ m
$y_2 = 2.8$ mm $= 2.8 \times 10^{-3}$ m

Substituting the values into the formula:

$\lambda = \dfrac{2 \times 0.66 \times 10^{-3} \times 2.8 \times 10^{-3}}{5 \times 1.4}$

$\lambda = \dfrac{3.696 \times 10^{-6}}{7}$

$\lambda = 0.528 \times 10^{-6}$ m

$\lambda = 5280 \times 10^{-10}$ m $= 5280 \ \text{\AA}$

Answer: $5280 \ \text{Å}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: In Young's double slit experiment, the wavelength of light used is $\lambda$. The intensity on the screen at a point for path difference '$\lambda$' is 'X'. The intensity at the point for path difference $\left(\dfrac{\lambda}{6}\right)$ is ($\cos 180^\circ = -1$, $\cos 30^\circ = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$)
questions.solution:
The phase difference $\phi$ is related to the path difference $\Delta x$ by the formula $\phi = \dfrac{2\pi}{\lambda} \Delta x$

The intensity at any point on the screen is given by $I = I_{max} \cos^2\left(\dfrac{\phi}{2}\right)$

For a path difference $\Delta x = \lambda$, the phase difference is $\phi = \dfrac{2\pi}{\lambda} \times \lambda = 2\pi$

The intensity is $I_1 = I_{max} \cos^2\left(\dfrac{2\pi}{2}\right) = I_{max} \cos^2(\pi) = I_{max}$

Given that $I_1 = X$, we have $I_{max} = X$

For a path difference $\Delta x = \dfrac{\lambda}{6}$, the phase difference is $\phi = \dfrac{2\pi}{\lambda} \times \dfrac{\lambda}{6} = \dfrac{\pi}{3}$

The intensity at this point is $I_2 = I_{max} \cos^2\left(\dfrac{\pi/3}{2}\right) = I_{max} \cos^2\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right)$

Substituting $I_{max} = X$ and $\cos\left(\dfrac{\pi}{6}\right) = \cos 30^\circ = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$:

$I_2 = X \left(\dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\right)^2 = \dfrac{3X}{4}$

Answer: $\dfrac{3X}{4}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q:
Which one of the following statements regarding pitch of sound is 'WRONG' ?
(A) Pitch refers to sharpness of sound.
(B) Tone refers to the single frequency of that wave.
(C) High pitch sound need not be louder.
(D) In general male sound is sharper than that of a female.
questions.solution:
Pitch is the characteristic of sound that determines its shrillness or sharpness, which depends on the frequency of the sound wave. A higher frequency corresponds to a higher pitch and a sharper sound.

A sound of a single frequency is called a tone.

Pitch and loudness are independent characteristics; pitch depends on frequency, whereas loudness depends on the amplitude of the sound wave. Thus, a high pitch sound need not be louder.

In general, the vocal cords of females are shorter and vibrate at a higher frequency compared to males. Therefore, a female's voice has a higher pitch and is sharper than a male's voice.

Statement D claims that male sound is sharper than that of a female, which is incorrect.

Answer: D

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A set of $14$ tuning forks is arranged in a series of increasing frequencies. Each fork produces '$x$' beats per second with the preceding fork and the last fork is an octave of the first fork. If the seventh fork has the frequency of $114$ Hz, the value of $x$ is
questions.solution:
Let the frequency of the first tuning fork be $f_1$.

Since each fork produces $x$ beats per second with the preceding fork and the frequencies are in increasing order, the frequencies form an arithmetic progression with a common difference of $x$.

The frequency of the $n$-th tuning fork is given by $f_n = f_1 + (n - 1)x$.

The frequency of the 14th tuning fork is $f_{14} = f_1 + 13x$.

It is given that the last fork is an octave of the first fork, which means $f_{14} = 2f_1$.

Substituting this into the equation, we get $2f_1 = f_1 + 13x \Rightarrow f_1 = 13x$.

The frequency of the 7th tuning fork is given as $114$ Hz.

Using the formula for the 7th fork, $f_7 = f_1 + 6x$.

Substituting $f_1 = 13x$, we get $f_7 = 13x + 6x = 19x$.

Equating this to the given frequency, $19x = 114$.

Solving for $x$, we get $x = \dfrac{114}{19} = 6$.

Answer: $6$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A tuning fork gives $5$ beats per second with a $33$ cm length of sonometer wire. If the length of the wire is shortened by $1$ cm, the number of beats is still the same. The frequency of the fork is
questions.solution:
Let the frequency of the tuning fork be $n$.

The frequency of a sonometer wire is inversely proportional to its length, $f \propto \dfrac{1}{L}$.

Let $f_1$ and $f_2$ be the frequencies of the wire for lengths $L_1 = 33$ cm and $L_2 = 32$ cm respectively.

Since $L_2 \lt L_1$, we have $f_2 \gt f_1$.

The tuning fork gives $5$ beats per second with both lengths. Thus, $f_1$ must be less than $n$ and $f_2$ must be greater than $n$.

$n - f_1 = 5 \Rightarrow f_1 = n - 5$

$f_2 - n = 5 \Rightarrow f_2 = n + 5$

Using the relation $f_1 L_1 = f_2 L_2$:

$(n - 5) \times 33 = (n + 5) \times 32$

$33n - 165 = 32n + 160$

$n = 325$ Hz

Answer: $325$ Hz

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The third overtone of a closed pipe of length '$L_c$' has the same frequency as the third overtone of the open pipe of length '$L_0$'. Both the pipes have same diameters. The ratio $L_c : L_0$ is equal to
questions.solution:
For a closed pipe, the frequency of the $n$-th overtone is given by $f_c = (2n + 1) \dfrac{v}{4L_c}$.

For the third overtone ($n = 3$), the frequency is $f_c = 7 \dfrac{v}{4L_c}$.

For an open pipe, the frequency of the $n$-th overtone is given by $f_o = (n + 1) \dfrac{v}{2L_0}$.

For the third overtone ($n = 3$), the frequency is $f_o = 4 \dfrac{v}{2L_0} = \dfrac{2v}{L_0}$.

Given that the frequencies of the third overtones are equal:

$7 \dfrac{v}{4L_c} = \dfrac{2v}{L_0}$

$\dfrac{L_c}{L_0} = \dfrac{7}{8}$

The ratio $L_c : L_0$ is $7:8$.

Answer: $7:8$

questions.q: The spring is initially in unstretched condition. It is first stretched by a length '$x$' and the work done is $W_1$. Then again it is stretched by further length '$x$' when the work done is $W_2$. The value of $W_2$ is given by
questions.solution:
Work done in stretching a spring from its natural length to an extension $x$ is given by $W_1 = \dfrac{1}{2}kx^2$.

When the spring is further stretched by a length $x$, the total extension becomes $2x$.

Total work done from the natural length to an extension $2x$ is $W = \dfrac{1}{2}k(2x)^2 = 4 \left(\dfrac{1}{2}kx^2\right) = 4W_1$.

Work done in the second step is $W_2 = W - W_1 = 4W_1 - W_1 = 3W_1$.

Answer: $3W_1$
